exercises.name: Muscle up
exercises.description:
The body is then explosively pulled up by the arms in a radial pull-up, with greater speed than a regular pull-up. When the bar approaches the upper chest, the wrists are swiftly flexed to bring the forearms above the bar. The body is leaned forward, and the elbows are straightened by activating the triceps. The routine is considered complete when the bar is at the level of the waist and the arms are fully straight.

To dismount, the arms are bent at the elbow, and the body is lowered to the floor, and the exercise can be repeated.

As a relatively advanced exercise, muscle-ups are typically first learned with an assistive kip. The legs swing (kip) up and provide momentum to assist in the explosive upward force needed to ascend above the bar. More advanced athletes can perform a strict variation of the muscle-up which is done slowly, without any kip. This variation begins with a still dead hang and uses isometric muscle contraction to ascend above the bar in a slow, controlled fashion.

exercises.name: box jumps
exercises.description: Jump from a standing position onto the box, stretch your body, then step down again (do not jump)

exercises.name: Frog stand
exercises.description:
Starting position:

  • Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing forward, facing a wall or bench for support if needed.
  • Bend your knees into a squat position.
  • Place your hands on the ground in front of you, shoulder-width apart, with your fingers spread wide.
  • Make sure your elbows are under your shoulders and your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.

Upward phase:

  • Push with your feet and hands to lift your body off the ground.
  • Straighten your legs and arms, keeping your body aligned.
  • Engage your core and glutes to maintain the position.
  • If needed, rest your knees on the wall or bench for assistance.

exercises.name: Counterclockwise neck circles
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Start sitting or standing. Drop your head down, bringing your chin toward your chest, but not pushing.

Steps:

In a slower fluid motion and with your head relaxed and not pushing in any direction:

  1. lean toward your left shoulder.
  2. then bring your head back, facing up.
  3. then lean toward your right shoulder.4.and back toward the starting position.

Keep repeating this as part of one slower fluid motion.

exercises.name: Kneeling Superman
exercises.description:
• Push one foot back until leg fully extended, concentrating on the having the foot high and pushed back as if pulled.

  • Extend arm forward with focus having the shoulder high up.

Unilateral and static hold.

exercises.name: Rowing seated, narrow grip
exercises.description:
• Tighten muscles
  • Controlled movement
  • Slow movement
  • Keep upper body upright
  • Do not lean back
  • Pull toward chest

exercises.name: Bent High Pulls
exercises.description: Bend over slightly while holding two dumbbells.  Pull the dumbbells up to your chest, keeping your elbows as high as you can.

exercises.name: Upright Row w/ Dumbbells
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your body. Keep your palms towards your body. Lift you hands straight up until your hands are under your chin, then lower them. Repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Dumbbell Lateral Raise with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Windshield Wipers
exercises.description: Hang from a pull-up bar, raise your legs to the ceiling. Move lower body from left to right with straight legs like a windshield wiper

exercises.name: Cable Rear-Delt Fly (single arm)
exercises.description: Cable rear delt fly (single arm): Stand sideways to a cable machine with the handle set around shoulder height. With a slight bend in the elbow, pull the handle out and back in a wide arc so the upper arm moves away from the body. Keep your torso still and focus on the rear delt doing the work. Use light to moderate weight and controlled reps.

exercises.name: Drag Pushdown
exercises.description:
1. Starting position for this rope pushdown is standing facing a cable machine with the handles of a rope attachment in both hands and feet shoulder width apart.
  2. Hinge forward slightly at the hips maintaining an upright chest and bring the shoulders and elbows behind the body so that when you push down on the cable attachments, you can get a fully contracted triceps long head.
  3. Drag the cable machine rope attachment as close to the body as possible and straighten your elbows until lockout.

exercises.name: DB Cross Body Hammer Curls
exercises.description: Hammer curl with a neutral grip, curling the dumbbell across your body towards the opposite shoulder. Works the brachialis in particular.

exercises.name: Kettlebell sumo high pull
exercises.description:
A compound exercise combining elements of a sumo deadlift and a high pull. It targets the posterior chain, particularly the glutes, hamstrings, and upper back. The sumo stance increases hip engagement, while the high pull adds an explosive element, promoting power development.

  • Stand upright overtop of a kettlebell with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart angled out slightly.
  • Maintain a braced core and neutral spine throughout the exercise.
  • Hinge your hips backward and extend your arms to grab ahold the kettlebell with a double overhand grip.
  • With you lower legs nearly vertical to the ground, extend your hips to raise the kettlebell with your elbows high keeping it close to your body.
  • Once the kettlebell has reached shoulder height, lower back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Flat Machine Press
exercises.description:
Execution

  1. Start position:

    • Elbows bent at roughly 90°, hands just outside your chest.
    • Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.

  2. Pressing phase (concentric):

    • Push the handles forward until your arms are almost fully extended — don’t lock out.
    • Focus on squeezing your chest at the end of the movement.

  3. Returning phase (eccentric):

    • Slowly bring the handles back toward your chest, feeling the stretch in your pecs.
    • Maintain tension — don’t let the weight stack touch down between reps.

exercises.name: Quadratus Lumborum Stretch (Custom)
exercises.description: Stand and side-bend slowly to one side, feel a gentle stretch along the waist, hold for thirty seconds, switch sides, move gently and stop if you feel sharp pain.

exercises.name: Reverse V-Squat
exercises.description:
Step into the V-squat machine facing the pad, the opposite way from the regular V-squat, so that your chest rests against the pad and your shoulders sit under the shoulder pads. Place your feet on the platform about shoulder width apart and release the safety.

Brace your core and lower yourself by bending your knees and pushing the hips back until your thighs are roughly parallel to the platform. Drive back up through the heels without locking out the knees.

Compared to the regular V-squat, the reversed position shifts the emphasis towards the glutes and hamstrings.

exercises.name: Hammercurls on Cable
exercises.description:
Take a cable in your hands (palms parallel, point to each other), the body is straight. Bend the arms and bring the weight up with a fast movement. Without any pause bring it back down with a slow, controlled movement, but don't stretch completely your arms.

Don't swing your body during the exercise, the biceps should do all the work here. The elbows are at your side and don't move.

exercises.name: Radio Taiso
exercises.description:
Video can be found here : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGPBSqxKGAc

Full-body mobility and dynamic warm-up routine (3–5 minutes) to prepare joints, muscles, and the cardiovascular system for workout.

Movement Flow:

Deep Breathing & Arm Raises: Inhale while raising arms laterally overhead, exhale as you lower them.

Knee Bends: Soft, rhythmic knee flexions synchronized with arm swings.

Arm Circles: Large full-range arm rotations forward, then backward to open up the chest and shoulder girdle.

Chest Expansion: Cross arms in front of the chest and open wide to the sides.

Side Bends: Reach overhead to stretch the lateral torso left and right with a smooth side flexion.

Forward & Back Bends: Gently hinge at the hips to reach forward, then return upright with a mild spinal extension.

Torso Twists: Swing arms side-to-side to rotate the spine and loosen the core.

Ankle Mobility / Light Bounces: Soft heel lifts or light bouncing on toes to warm up lower leg joints and tendons.

exercises.name: Active Hang
exercises.description: A static hold from a pull-up bar with straight elbows and actively depressed, stabilized shoulders. Grip a secure bar and let your body hang under control. Keep your elbows straight and gently draw your shoulders down, away from your ears. Maintain this active shoulder position without pulling up, swinging, or repeatedly moving the shoulder blades. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier if your grip opens, shoulder control deteriorates, or pain occurs. Record actual seconds, grip, and any assistance used. This is distinct from a relaxed passive dead hang or a moving scapular pull-up.

exercises.name: Calf raises, right leg
exercises.description:
1. Stand on the floor or on the edge of a step to increase the range of movement.
  2. Raise one foot.
  3. Lift your heel until you're standing on your toes.
  4. (variable) Stay in this position for three seconds
  5. Slowly lower your foot until you almost touch the ground with your heel - don't slam your foot!

exercises.name: Barbell Lunges Standing
exercises.description:
Put barbell on the back of your shoulders. Stand upright, then take the first step forward. Step should bring you forward so that your supporting legs knee can touch the floor. Then stand back up and repeat with the other leg.

Remember to keep good posture.

exercises.name: Chin tuck
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Sit or stand with your back straight.

Steps:

  1. Use fingers on your chin to slowly tuck your chin in, moving your head back to align it with your spine.
  2. Hold for 5 seconds.
  3. Go back to normal head position and repeat.

exercises.name: Cable Shrug-In
exercises.description: Attach a D-handle to each of two low pulleys, stand between them and shrug your shoulders up and inwards, using your upper traps.

exercises.name: Calves foam roller
exercises.description: Move your calves slowly over the foam roller

exercises.name: Side lateral raise - Back (Cable)
exercises.description: on a cable rack do a side lateral raise with the cable behind you. focus on tension in the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl
exercises.description: Cable curl with the shoulder extended backwards, which puts the biceps in a stretched position at the start of the movement.

exercises.name: TRX roll out
exercises.description: Hold the handles in your hands, extend your arms and keep them parallel at chest height. The movement you need to perform is to open your arms in line with your shoulders while leaning your body forward. Try not to extend your shoulders beyond 90°, and keep your abdominal muscles and glutes contracted. Muscles involved: transverse abdominis, rectus abdominis and spinal erectors.

exercises.name: Isometric Squat to Failure
exercises.description:
sometric Squat to Failure: A Strength Training Technique

Definition

The isometric squat to failure is a variation of the squat exercise where you hold a static squat position at a specific angle, maintaining the position until your muscles can no longer sustain the contraction.

exercises.name: Typewriter Pull-ups
exercises.description: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width. Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar. At the top position, instead of going straight down, shift your body to one side by extending one arm while keeping the other arm bent. Move smoothly from one side to the other, like a typewriter motion, before lowering yourself back down. This exercise increases time under tension and strengthens the lats, biceps, and shoulders while building unilateral pulling strength.

exercises.name: Fly With Cable
exercises.description: cable machine, two steps forward, straight back

exercises.name: Cable Tri Extension - Internal Rotation
exercises.description: single arm exercise with cable held at opposite shoulder with elbow bent. Turn towards the cable, and the straighten the elbow across the body.

exercises.name: Boxing
exercises.description: Bag workout for boxing skill development and cardio improvement

exercises.name: Standing Dowel Shoulder press
exercises.description: Mobility - prone dowel press or standing dowel shoulder press alternating between front andback

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Triceps Pushdown with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Step Calf Stretch
exercises.description: Stand on a step or a sturdy raised surface with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging off, holding a rail or wall for balance. Let one or both heels drop below the level of the step until you feel a stretch through the calf, and hold. Keep the knee straight to stretch the gastrocnemius, or bend the knee slightly to bias the soleus lower down. Hold for the prescribed time, typically 30 seconds, without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg at a time.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Close-grip Bench Press
exercises.description: Perform a standard bench press on the smith machine, but have your hands on the bar about shoulder width apart, and keep your elbows close to your body.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
exercises.description: Plank with stomach towards ceiling

exercises.name: Single leg press
exercises.description: Strength training exercise where you push a weight away from your body using one leg at a time on a leg press machine. It helps to improve leg strength, balance, and muscular symmetry by isolating each leg individually. This exercise is particularly useful for identifying and correcting muscle imbalances between your legs.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.description: A dip is an upper-body strength exercise. Narrow, shoulder-width dips primarily train the triceps, with major synergists being the anterior deltoid, the pectoralis muscles (sternal, clavicular, and minor), and the rhomboid muscles of the back (in that order).[1] Wide arm training places additional emphasis on the pectoral muscles, similar in respect to the way a wide grip bench press would focus more on the pectorals and less on the triceps.

exercises.name: Sumo Squats
exercises.description:
Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders, with your toes pointed out at a 45 degree angle and barbell on your shoulder.

While keeping your back straight, descend slowly by bending at the knees and hips as if you are sitting down (squatting).

Lower yourself until your quadriceps and hamstrings are parallel to the floor.

Return to the starting position by pressing upwards and extending your legs while maintaining an equal distribution of weight on your forefoot and heel.

exercises.name: Cable Wrist Pronation
exercises.description: Attach a strap or handle to a cable at hand height so the cable pulls your palm toward facing up. Keep your elbow bent at your side and still. Rotate your forearm so the palm turns down against the cable, then let it rotate back slowly. This builds pronation strength for rolling an opponent's hand in arm wrestling.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description:
1. Begin with a bar loaded on the ground. Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide, near the collars. Bend at the hips to grip the bar. The arms should be directly below the shoulders, inside the legs, and you can use a pronated grip, a mixed grip, or hook grip. Relax the shoulders, which in effect lengthens your arms.
  2. Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the back half of your feet. Extend through the hips and knees.
  3. As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
  4. Return the weight to the ground by bending at the hips and controlling the weight on the way down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift
exercises.description: Lower your dumbbell to the ground between your legs. Assume a wide stance and with a straight back squat down. With the dumbbell standing upright, grip it by the top of the ‘head’ (picture 1).Keeping your chest up and core braced, push the floor away, driving back upwards to a standing position (picture 2). Repeat. If you can easily achieve 20-30 reps, use two dumbbells.

exercises.name: Hand Gripper Squeeze
exercises.description: Hold a spring hand gripper deep in your palm. Squeeze until the handles touch, hold for a second, then open slowly. Use a gripper strength you can close for the target reps. This builds crushing grip strength for holding on in arm wrestling and in pulling exercises.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Row with Rotation (Floor)
exercises.description:
Go into a one-legged kneeling position and grab the cable from the lowest position.

Rotate the upper torso to get into the starting position and bend the upper torso a little bit sidewise.

Place the unused hand on the knee.

Pull the cable while rotating the upper torso.

exercises.name: Leg Press Toe Press
exercises.description: Move the leg press using your calves by placing your feet at the bottom of the platform.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description:
Kneel in a lunge position with one knee on the floor and the other foot in front, hands on your hips.

Keep your torso upright, squeeze the glute of the back leg and push your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip and thigh. Hold, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Weighted neck flexion
exercises.description: Weighted neck flexion is an isolation exercise designed to strengthen the anterior (front) neck flexor muscles by bringing your chin toward your chest against external resistance (most commonly a light weight plate, resistance band, or neck harness).

exercises.name: Neck CARs
exercises.description: Controlled Articular Rotations. Slow full circles 3 each way. Cervical mobility.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand
exercises.description: Handstand against a wall for support (chest facing wall).

exercises.name: Calf Press Using Leg Press Machine
exercises.description:
Put  the balls of your feet on an extended leg press pad.  Use your calves to press the weight by flexing your feet/toes into a pointed position, and releasing back into a relaxed position.

This exercise builds mass and strength in the Gastrocnemius and Soleus muscles as well, if not better, than any calf exercise.

exercises.name: Side Straight-Arm Pulldown (Cable)
exercises.description:
Keep your torso still, pulling the handle down along your side using the outer lat.

Don’t twist your body or rotate your torso to cheat the rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Rising
exercises.description: Stand tall with your arm hanging straight down by your side. Hold a dumbbell by one end of the handle so the weighted end points forward and your thumb is on top. Keep the arm completely still and tip the weighted end up toward the ceiling using only the wrist, then lower it slowly. This trains radial deviation, the riser used in arm wrestling. Slide your hand further from the weight to make it harder.

exercises.name: Rocking Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: Set your feet below the rope and lean your upper body towards the rope. Set one foot back. Push down the rope and lean your entire body back onto the rear foot as you push down to get your hands behind your body. Don't forget to bring your chest to the front during the pushdown. As you release the rope slowly, lean your body back onto the front foot.

exercises.name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Flatten your lower back against the floor by tilting your pelvis posteriorly, engaging your abs and glutes. Hold 5 seconds, release. This retrains pelvic positioning to counter anterior pelvic tilt.
aliases: Pelvic Tilt Drill / Supine Pelvic Tilt

exercises.name: Fingerboard 20 mm edge
exercises.description: Hang for 10 seconds on a fingerboard with a 20 mm edge

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description:
1. Take a seat on the machine with your feet planted, a little wider than shoulder width. Drive the heels, and squeeze the glutes. Grab onto the cable handle.
  2. Sit up tall with a slight bend through the knees. Tighten up the abs and low back to maintain a perpendicular angle to the floor with your torso.
  3. Roll the shoulders back and down. Squeeze them together as you row, thinking about pinching a pencil in between them. As you do this, pull the handle back towards you, landing right above your belly button.
  4. Pause here for a moment before returning the handle, still squeezing the shoulder blades. Once you've returned the weight to the stack, then allow the shoulder blades to relax, without pulling the torso forward.
  5. Repeat the movement.

exercises.name: Straight-arm Pull Down (bar Attachment)
exercises.description: Use the straight bar attachment on a high pulley. Grasp the two ends of the bar with your palms facing downward and your arms straight out in front of you. Pull your hands down towards your hips, while keeping your arms straight, then raise them back up to the starting position.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.description:
1. Hold a dumbbell, barbell weight or something else that is heavy with both hands, but make sure it is not too heavy and you are able to keep in form.
  2. Lean back to a 45-degree angle from the floor. For an extra challenge, lift your feet off the floor.
  3. Rotate your arms to one side to the same level as your chest, touch the floor for a little extra challenge, and then do the same to the other side. When you're back in your original position after doing both sides it will count as 1 rep.

exercises.name: Kickstand RDL
exercises.description: use non-working leg's toes to help with balance and perform an RDL.

exercises.name: No Leg Drive Dumbbell Chest Press
exercises.description: Set up for a normal Dumbbell chest press but lift your leg ups straight or put them on another bench to remove the leg drive.

exercises.name: Seated Bench Press
exercises.description: Set up the chest press machine so that the grips are aligned with your lower chest when you sit down. Make sure you're sitting with your back flat against the seat. Grab a handle in each hand, stick your chest out, and keep your head against the headrest. Breathe deeply and slowly push the handles forward until your arms are almost fully extended. Pause just before the lockout, then slowly return the handles to the starting position. Pause just before the handles come to a complete stop and perform another repetition.

exercises.name: Kelso Shrugs
exercises.description:
Kelso shrugs are a variation of scapular shrugs designed primarily to train scapular retraction, with particular emphasis on the middle trapezius, rhomboids, and, secondarily, the lower trapezius. Unlike conventional shrugs, the goal is not to elevate the shoulders toward the ears, but rather to pull the shoulder blades backward.

They are typically performed with the chest supported on an incline bench, using either dumbbells or a barbell:

  1. Lie face down on an incline bench, with your arms extended toward the floor.
  2. Keep your elbows almost completely locked throughout the movement.
  3. Starting with the shoulder blades slightly protracted, retract them, trying to bring them closer together.
  4. Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench; avoid turning the movement into a row by extending your torso.
  5. Briefly hold the fully retracted position, then return in a controlled manner, allowing the shoulder blades to separate.

exercises.name: Plank Reach
exercises.description: Position your body in plank position, keeping your eyes on the ground. Raise one arm in front of you and return it. Repeat with the other arm. Raise and return slowly while keeping your body as still as possible.

exercises.name: Snatch OL
exercises.description:
Olympic lift snatch

  • Pull barbell from ground to overhead lockout using a wide grip and overhead squat.
  • Move bar slowly until cleared knees then explosively extend hips, pull bar up and dive under the bar
  • Catch bar overhead with straight arms
  • Push head forward during lockout

exercises.name: Recumbent Bike
exercises.description: For this exercise Recumbent Bike is needed. You just sit on it, set level and time and start the workout

exercises.name: Barbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Position barbell overhead with narrow overhand grip.

Lower forearm behind upper arm with elbows remaining overhead. Extend forearm overhead. Lower and repeat.

exercises.name: Dead Bug Breathing (Custom)
exercises.description: Lie on your back, breathe in fully, let the ribs sink down, press the lower back into the floor, exhale slowly while keeping intra-abdominal pressure, five reps per set.

exercises.name: Seated Cable chest fly
exercises.description:
1. Place a bench between two cable pulleys and adjust the pulleys so they are at chest/shoulder height when you are seated.
  2. Grab the handles with a neutral grip and lean against the upright backrest.
  3. Bring your arms together in front of your chest in a controlled motion, focusing on squeezing your chest muscles. Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement.
  4. Pause briefly at the top position.
  5. Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position while maintaining control of the movement.
  6. Repeat for reps.

exercises.name: Unilateral Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Extend one leg while laying down and start raising your body with one leg touching the ground through the heel.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press, on Multi Press
exercises.description:
The exercise is basically the same as with a free barbell:

Sit on a bench, the back rest should be almost vertical. Take a bar with a shoulder wide grip and bring it down to chest height. Press the weight up, but don't stretch the arms completely. Go slowly down and repeat.

exercises.name: YTW Raises
exercises.description: The YTW exercise for scapular retraction is designed to strengthen the inter-scapular muscles between your shoulder blades, to help retract or pull your shoulders back, helping to maintain proper upright posture.

exercises.name: TRX/Rings Y Raise
exercises.description:
1. Set TRX straps or rings at about mid-chest to waist height. Stand facing the anchor and hold one handle or ring in each hand.
  2. Walk the feet toward the anchor and lean back until the arms are extended in front of you and the body forms a straight line from head to heels. Palms face each other or slightly down.
  3. Brace the core and glutes. Keep the shoulders down and the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
  4. With a soft bend in the elbows, raise the arms up and out into a Y shape overhead, so the hands finish roughly in line with the ears and wider than the shoulders.
  5. Reach long through the arms without shrugging. Pause briefly at the top with control.
  6. Lower the arms under control back to the start position in front of the body, then repeat.

Keep tension in the straps throughout. A more upright stance makes the movement easier; a deeper lean makes it harder.

exercises.name: Rope Pullover/row
exercises.description: Set up bench in front of cable row machine. Lean over bench to do a row/pullover with rope that targets lats. See picture.

exercises.name: Diagonal Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
You sit at the bench press device, back slightly tilted to the back. The bar should be about 20 cm in front of you. Then you push the bar and take it back again, as you would with a bench press.

In this position you strain your chest muscles a lot less, which is nice if you want to train, but your chest hasn't recovered yet.

exercises.name: Box squat
exercises.description:
1. Set up the box: Position the box behind you, about 3 feet from a squat rack if you're using a barbell. Choose a height that allows you to squat down and gently tap your glutes on the box with your back straight.
  2. Stand with proper form: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward. Engage your core and keep your back neutral. If using a barbell, rack it at shoulder height.
  3. Lower down: Sit back as if going to sit on a chair, bending your knees and lowering your hips towards the box. Keep your core tight and back straight throughout the movement.
  4. Controlled descent: Descend in a controlled manner until your glutes gently touch the box. Don't plop down.
  5. Pause and press up: Briefly pause at the bottom with your back straight and core engaged. Then, press through your heels to drive yourself back up to the starting position.

Improvements in coordination, balance and endurance, toning of the leg and buttock muscles and an overall increase in bone density eliminating the risk of osteoporosis.

exercises.name: Cool-Down Swim
exercises.description: Swim at an easy, unhurried pace — freestyle, backstroke, or just floating/gliding — with zero focus on technique or drills. The only goal here is to let your heart rate come down gradually and your muscles relax before you get out of the pool.

exercises.name: Supported Split Squat
exercises.description:
Stand in a split stance with one foot about a stride in front of the other, and hold on to a stable support such as a rack, a wall or the back of a chair.

Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees until the back knee almost touches the floor. Keep your upper body upright and the front heel on the floor, then push through the front foot back up. Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up. Complete all repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Drop Curl
exercises.description: Drop curls in a modified position at a slow pace effectively engage the brachialis for arm width. Starting position is with both arms in a slight angle towards each other at chest height with a dumbbell in each hand. Lower one dumbbell close to full extended arm position slowly and in a controlled manner during the first half of the curl, then curl it back up to starting position, while the other dumbbell stays at its starting position. Now lower the other dumbbell down. This keeps tension on the brachialis. As we pass the 90deg mark on our way down, the biceps will take over the work.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip pull-ups or TRX rows
exercises.description:
• Pull-Up: Vertical Pull — Focuses more on the Lats (back width).

    TRX Row: Horizontal Pull — Focuses more on the Rhomboids/Traps (mid-back thickness and posture).

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Leg Extension with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: L Hold
exercises.description: Hold the L position for as long as possible

exercises.name: L-sit
exercises.description:
Sit on the ground with your legs together and your arms by your sides. Push your body off the ground using your hands, maintaining the same sitting position so that your legs are straight and your feet do not touch the floor.

Hold for as long as required.

exercises.name: Inverted Lat Pull Down
exercises.description: The Inverted Lat Pull Down (most commonly known as the Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down) is a variation of the standard exercise that uses an underhand (supinated) grip with hands at shoulder-width. This position shifts more emphasis to the lower lats and increases biceps involvement, often allowing for a greater range of motion and a deeper squeeze at the bottom of the movement.

exercises.name: Hack Squats (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Hack Squats with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Gluteus
exercises.description: Sit on the foam roller and slowly roll back and forth over your glutes with moderate pressure.

exercises.name: Open Book
exercises.description:
Basic exercise

  • Focus: enhances thoracic mobility and spinal segmentation while opening the shoulders and chest.
  • **Position:**kneeling on the floor with your right side facing a wall. Hips are square and stable, with the right knee down and the left foot forward. Lengthen your spine and align your head comfortably. Begin with your arms relaxed and open in front of your chest, palms facing each other and hands apart.
  • Inhale to initiate the movement, allowing your left arm —the one farther from the wall— to open outward and backward. Lead the twist from your thoracic spine, rotating your upper back progressively while keeping your pelvis still.
  • Exhale as you complete the rotation, guiding your left hand toward the wall as your gaze follows your hand.
  • Return by inhaling and slowly bringing your arm forward, reversing the spinal rotation segment by segment.
  • Repeat on the opposite side.

Progression

  • **Position:**kneeling on the floor with your right side facing a wall. Left knee down and right foot forward.
  • Before the basic exercise: inhale, exhalewhile moving the right arm along the wall with a circle upwards and backwards, inhalewhile bringing back the arm.
  • Basic exercise.
  • Repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Adductors
exercises.description: Lie face down with one leg bent out to the side and the foam roller under the inner thigh. Slowly roll back and forth over your adductors with moderate pressure.

exercises.name: Shotgun Row
exercises.description:
1. Attach a single handle to a low cable.
  2. After selecting the correct weight, stand a couple feet back with a wide-split stance. Your arm should be extended and your shoulder forward. This will be your starting position.
  3. Perform the movement by retracting the shoulder and flexing the elbow. As you pull, supinate the wrist, turning the palm upward as you go.
  4. After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Incline DB Y-Raise
exercises.description:
1. Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit facing the bench, chest against the pad, with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
  2. Position your feet firmly on the ground for stability and let your arms hang down naturally with a slight bend in your elbows.
  3. Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
  4. Raise your arms forward and out to form a Y shape, keeping the movement controlled and your elbows slightly bent.
  5. Lift until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor and in line with your ears.
  6. Pause briefly at the top of the movement to engage your shoulder muscles fully, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
  7. Ensure the movement is slow and controlled during both the ascent and descent to maximize engagement of the deltoids and supporting muscles.
  8. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.

exercises.name: Back bridge
exercises.description: Lie on the floor with your back resting on the floor and your legs bent, feet flat on the floor, leaving about 20 cm between your feet and your buttocks. Your hands remain flat on the floor, pressed against your ears, with your fingers pointing toward your toes. Your elbows are bent and pointing toward the ceiling. This is the starting position. Now push your hips as high as you can, raising your body off the floor, and continue pushing through your hands, extending your elbows and knees, until your back is fully arched (lumbar bridge). Your head also comes off the floor and should be level with your elbows, looking back. This is the final position. The descent should be slow and controlled. Your spine should be in a convex curve. It's not good to lift your back off the floor; it should remain straight. It should be well rounded. You'll also notice a feeling of increased oxygenation in your back. After lifting off the floor, your hips should be very high, even above the level of your head. Your arms and legs should remain straight. It seems easy, but it requires a good level of flexibility. Breathing should be deep. This posture stretches the rib cage and puts pressure on the diaphragm. If the posture is performed correctly, breathing will be perfect. Never hold your breath during the exercise.

exercises.name: Patadas traseras
exercises.description:
The dumbbell kickback is a popular strength training exercise that targets the triceps muscles in the back of your upper arms. It helps strengthen and tone the triceps, contributing to overall arm strength and aesthetics.

Among the exercises that work the arm muscles, kickback and its variations are very effective. You can easily apply these exercises with dumbbells, cables or resistance bands.

exercises.name: Wrist rocks
exercises.description: Start on all fours with your palms flat on the floor. Slowly rock forward and backward, keeping your hands planted. Move only within a comfortable, pain-free wrist range to gently improve mobility and flexibility.

exercises.name: Low Box Squat - Wide Stance
exercises.description: Unrack the bar and set your stance wide, beyond your hips.  Push your hips back and sit down to a box that takes you below parallel.  Sit completely down, do not touch and go.  Then explosively stand up.  Stay tight in your upper back and torso throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Wide Push-Up
exercises.description:
​A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to increase the emphasis on the outer chest muscles and shoulders.

  1. ​Setup: Place hands wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor.
  2. Lower: Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your core tight.
  3. ​Push: Drive through your palms to return to the start position.
  4. ​Form: Don't let your lower back sag; keep a straight line from head to heels.

exercises.name: 4-count burpees
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Stand straight, feet hip-width apart.

Steps:

  1. Squat low and support yourself on the floor with your hands between the knees and in front of your feet, your back straight.
  2. Keeping your hands on the floor, jump your legs backward into high plank position.
  3. Jump your feet forward to return to the squat position.
  4. Repeat.

exercises.name: Triceps Overhead (Dumbbell)
exercises.description:

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: The bar should go directly on your upper thigh, directly below your crotch. Your feet should be directly under your knees. Push your hips up so that you form a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Use a pad for comfort.

exercises.name: Cable glute extension
exercises.description: This exercise lets you work the upper, or larger, part of the glutes. For that reason, it should never be missing from your routine of isolated exercises for training the glutes. Stand in front of a cable machine and locate the low pulley. Then attach the ankle strap to work on the low pulley. As for your posture, you should stay upright at all times. Pay special attention to your back to keep it straight and avoid injury. It is advisable to hold on to the machine for better balance. With the leg that is holding the weight of the cable, perform a slow stretch backward without bending the knee.

exercises.name: Leg Wheel
exercises.description:
Lay on the back and lift legs in perpendicular fashion, keeping the knees together.

Start making small circles in one direction with both of your knees with very small range of motion, focusing on abs and keeping your back in contact with the floor.

exercises.name: Shoulder Flexion Wall Stretch
exercises.description: Place both hands against a wall above shoulder height. Step back and gently move the chest downward while reaching the arms overhead, keeping the back controlled. Hold a comfortable shoulder flexion stretch without forcing the range or arching the lower back.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Curls
exercises.description: Seated Dumbbell Curls are an effective bicep workout that isolates the muscles by stabilizing the upper body, reducing momentum that can detract from the exercise’s effectiveness. This exercise is performed sitting down with a dumbbell in each hand, focusing on controlled movement to maximize engagement of the bicep muscles.

exercises.name: Backward shoulder rotation
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Sit or stand with your back straight.

Steps:

  1. Place your hands on your shoulders.
  2. Repeatedly rotate both shoulder joints in a circular motion at a moderate pace.

exercises.name: Biceps Curls With Dumbbell
exercises.description:
Hold two dumbbells, the arms are streched, the hands are on your side, the palms face inwards. Bend the arms and bring the weight with a fast movement up. At the same time, rotate your arms by 90 degrees at the very beginning of the movement. At the highest point, rotate a little the weights further outwards. Without a pause, bring them down, slowly.

Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).

exercises.name: 2 Handed Kettlebell Swing
exercises.description:
1. Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, the kettlebell on the floor about 20-30 cm in front of your toes.
  2. Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in the knees and a flat back, and grip the handle with both hands.
  3. Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward explosively so that it swings forward and up to chest or shoulder height (Russian style, not overhead). Your arms stay straight and relaxed, the power comes from the hips.
  4. Let the kettlebell swing back down, hinge again as it passes between your legs and go straight into the next rep.

exercises.name: Core Rotation
exercises.description: Sit back, raise feet above the ground with knees bent and start rotating left and right with hands touching the ground every move.

exercises.name: Pause Hack Squats
exercises.description: Hack Squats but with a 1-2s pause at the bottom of the movement. This makes sure that there is no more elastic energy stored in the muscles.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Bench Press

exercises.name: Triceps stretch right
exercises.description: Put your right hand on your back, use your left hand to grab your right elbow and gently pull it. Hold this position for a few seconds.

exercises.name: Butterfly Sit Up
exercises.description: In this midrange exercise your arm muscles provide you with a little bit of momentum to help to get you off the ground. You also open them up in overhead position which engages the upper back. Start lying with feet flat on the ground, knees at an angle, arms crossed in towards your chest. Using your ab muscles, bring your upper body off the ground as you open your arms into goal post position, then slowly lower yourself back down to return to starting position.

exercises.name: Stroke-and-Roll Drill
exercises.description: Push off, swim a few strokes, and every breath roll fully onto your back for 2-3 breaths, then roll back into freestyle. This teaches you to rotate your body as a unit rather than just turning your head, and helps remove the fear of not having your face in the water.

exercises.name: Prone Leg Kickback (Custom)
exercises.description: Lie face down with legs straight, kick both legs back, squeeze the glutes, keep the lower back flat, move slowly under control, ten reps per set, breathe steadily.

exercises.name: elbow lever
exercises.description: ​A calisthenics static balance skill where the entire body is held straight and parallel to the ground, supported by tucking the elbows firmly into the abdomen or pelvic bones.

exercises.name: Hindu Squats
exercises.description:
Start with your feet shoulder width apart and arms slightly behind your back.

As you descend towards the floor, raise your heels off the ground, while keeping your back as vertical  as possible.

Upon attaining the bottom position, touch the hands to the heels.

Then stand up ending with the heels on the ground, arms extended in front of the chest then rowing into the start position.

exercises.name: Split squats right
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Stand with your back straight. Take a large step forward with your right leg.

Steps:

  1. Bring your pelvis down until you almost touch the floor with your left knee.
  2. Bring your pelvis back up.
  3. Repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row
exercises.description:
The Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row will involve the back, which means you can try a bit heavier weight. The catch is that you need to be able to control the weight for all the reps.

  1. Start by holding a pair of dumbbells with your feet shoulder-wide apart and your knees slightly bent.
  2. Hinge at your hips to lower your torse forward until it's almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat and maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
  3. Exhale as you row the dumbbells to your sides up to chest height, leading with your elbows until your upper arms are just past parallel to the floor and the dumbbells are at ribcage level.
  4. Slowly lower to the starting position and repeat. Keep your back flat all the time.

exercises.name: Torso rotation stretch
exercises.description:
The torso rotation stretch helps improve spinal mobility and relieves tension in the lower back and obliques. It can be performed standing or seated.

  1. Standing Variation: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your hands on your hips or extend your arms in front of you. Slowly rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips stable. Hold for a few seconds, then rotate to the opposite side.
  2. Seated Variation: Sit on a chair with your feet flat on the floor. Place one hand on the outside of your opposite thigh and gently twist your torso toward that side. Hold the stretch before switching sides.

exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a kettlebell in one hand and standing on one leg while bending forward to touch the kettlebell to the ground. It targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back while also improving balance and stability.

Pinch the hub with your fingertips on one side and your thumb on the other, then stand up and hold it for the set time. This builds thumb and pinch strength, which helps grip control in arm wrestling.

exercises.name: Dumbbell drag curls

exercises.name: Pike Hold (Floor)
exercises.description: A static bodyweight support with both hands and feet on the floor and hips raised in a pike position. Place your hands and feet securely on the floor, then raise your hips. Keep your elbows straight and actively push the floor away through your shoulders. Maintain a controlled, stationary position without bending your elbows, lowering your head for push-up repetitions, or raising your feet onto a surface. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier for loss of alignment, loss of active shoulder support, or pain. Record actual seconds, hand and foot spacing, and alignment. This is the floor variation, not a pike push-up or an elevated-feet pike hold.

It provides an effective way to improve endurance while strengthening the lower body. To use the machine, step onto the moving stairs, maintain an upright posture, and use the handrails for balance if needed. Adjust the speed and intensity to match your fitness level. This exercise helps improve cardiovascular health, burns calories, and enhances lower body muscle endurance.

exercises.name: Explosive Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Explosive Push-Ups

Start in a standard push-up position, lower your chest, then explosively push off the ground so your hands leave the floor. Land softly and immediately repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell donkey kick
exercises.description: The dumbbell donkey kick is an effective exercise for working the glute and hamstring muscles. This exercise is usually performed on all fours, using a dumbbell to add resistance. The steps for performing it correctly are described below. Starting position: Get on all fours on a mat, with your hands aligned under your shoulders and your knees aligned under your hips. Placing the dumbbell: Take a dumbbell and place it behind the knee of the leg you are going to lift. Make sure it is held securely to prevent it from falling during the exercise. Exercise: Inhale and, as you exhale, lift the leg with the dumbbell upward, keeping the knee bent at a 90-degree angle. Raise the leg until it is parallel to the floor, feeling the contraction in the glutes. Hold the position for one second at the top and then slowly lower the leg back to the starting position. Repetitions: Perform 10 to 15 repetitions per leg, making sure to maintain good form throughout the exercise. Sets: Complete 2 to 3 sets, depending on your fitness level.

exercises.name: Quadruped thoracic rotation left
exercises.description:
Starting position: Start kneeling on all fours, knees shoulder-width apart. Place your left hand behind your head while keeping your right hand outstretched and touching the floor. Steps:

  1. On inhale, move your left elbow toward your right hand, keeping your left hand behind your head.
  2. On exhale, move your left elbow to point up toward the ceiling.
  3. Repeat.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
exercises.description:
"The Y"

  • Position: Set an incline bench to 30-45 degrees. Lie face-down with your chest supported, keeping your head neutral or looking slightly down to avoid neck strain.
  • Grip: Hold light dumbbells with a neutral or thumbs-up grip (thumb pointing to the ceiling).
  • Movement: With straight or slightly bent elbows, raise the dumbbells up and out in a "Y" shape. Focus on moving the shoulders and shoulder blades rather than just lifting the arms.
  • Top Position: Squeeze the shoulder blades together and reach high, ensuring the arms are angled to form a "Y".
  • Control: Lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.description:
1. Stand facing away from a bench, couch or similar-height object.
  2. Extend one leg backwards, resting your foot "laces-down" on the edge of the bench.
  3. Lower yourself until your rear knee is on the floor and you are in a lunge position, with your torso hanging forwards slightly.
  4. Brace your core, tense your rear glute, and straighten up your torso to vertical, under control. Relax and repeat.

Repeat for the other leg, too.

exercises.name: Shrugs, Barbells
exercises.description:
Take a barbell and stand with a straight body, the arms are hanging freely in front of you. Lift from this position the shoulders as high as you can, but don't bend the arms during the movement. On the highest point, make a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds before returning slowly to the initial position.

When training with a higher weight, make sure that you still do the whole movement!

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Row
exercises.description:
1. Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
  2. Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
  3. Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
  4. Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Benchpress Dumbbells
exercises.description:
1. Setup and Starting Position: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically against each thigh. Carefully lean back while driving the dumbbells toward your chest with your knees.

  2. The “Leg Drive” and Posture: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your shoulder blades (press them together against the bench) and maintain a slight natural lumbar curve.

  3. Starting Position: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling. Your wrists should be aligned with your elbows. Rotate the dumbbells slightly inward (about 45 degrees) so that your elbows do not splay out too far to the sides, thereby protecting your shoulders.

  4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner toward the sides of your chest. Your elbows should lower at an angle of about 45–60 degrees relative to your body. Feel the stretch in the lower part of your chest.

  5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the weight upward in a slight arc (toward the center), without letting the dumbbells collide at the top or fully locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension. Exhale as you lift.

exercises.name: Quad Sets
exercises.description:
What Are Quad Sets?

Quad sets are a fundamental exercise used in knee rehabilitation. They focus on strengthening the quadriceps muscles located at the front of the thigh. This exercise is particularly beneficial for individuals recovering from knee injuries or surgeries.

How to Perform Quad Sets Steps to Execute Quad Sets
  1. Positioning: Sit or lie down with your legs straight.
  2. Tightening: Tighten the quadriceps muscles while keeping the leg straight. You should see the kneecap move upward.
  3. Holding: Maintain the contraction for about 5 seconds.
  4. Releasing: Relax the muscle after the hold.
  5. Repetitions: Aim for 10 to 15 repetitions, gradually increasing as strength improves.
Tips for Effective Quad Sets
  • Ensure no other muscles are contracting to assist the quadriceps.
  • Perform the exercise on a flat surface, like a bed or couch, with a towel or pillow under your heel for comfort.
  • It is recommended to do these exercises multiple times a day, especially during the early stages of recovery.
Benefits of Quad Sets
  • Restores Muscle Function: Helps rebuild strength in the quadriceps.
  • Improves Stability: Enhances stability in the knee joint.
  • Increases Range of Motion: Aids in regaining mobility after injury or surgery.

Incorporating quad sets into your rehabilitation routine can significantly aid in recovery and improve overall knee function.

exercises.name: Meadows Row

Rest the other forearm on the forward leg. Start this movement by driving the elbow behind you while retracting the shoulder-blade. Keep the working shoulder down. Pull toward your back hip until the elbow is level with your torso.

exercises.name: Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Set a cable pulley at the lowest position and attach a single handle. Stand side-on to the machine, hold the frame with your near hand and lean your body away so you hang at an angle. With the far hand, grasp the handle in front of your hips and raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow. Lower slowly. The lean increases tension on the side delts at the bottom of the movement. Complete all reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Crunches With Cable

exercises.name: Clean and Press
exercises.description:
• The First Pull: Lift the bar from the floor to knee-height by driving with the legs, keeping the angle of your back constant.
  • The "Power" Position: As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively shrug and extend your hips to create vertical momentum.
  • The Quick Elbow Turnover: In the catch phase, rotate your elbows rapidly under the bar to create a "shelf" on your front deltoids.
  • The Vertical Press: Press the bar in a straight line; your head should shift slightly forward once the bar clears your forehead to reach full lockout.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
Distribute your body weight evenly on all knees and arms. Keep the torso stable, with the abdomen engaged and the lumbar spine straight without twisting the back (imagine: a glass on your lower back won't fall off). Raise one leg outwards without twisting it.

Pay attention to the right angle at the hips and knees. Always train both sides of the body.

To increase resistance, a resistance band can be used.

exercises.name: Dumbell Tate Press
exercises.description:
1. Set Up: Lie flat with a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms straight up over your chest as if you were at the top of a dumbbell bench press
  2. Starting Position: Position the dumbbells so they are touching or very close together with a pronated grip (palms facing your feet and thumbs facing each other)
  3. Lowering: Without moving your upper arms or shoulders, bend your elbows and flare them outward to the sides. Lower the inner ends of the dumbbells toward the center of your chest
  4. Touch and Pause: Gently touch the dumbbells to your chest. Do not rest the weight on your body; maintain constant tension in your triceps
  5. Press: Forcefully extend your elbows to return the dumbbells to the starting position. Focus on "pushing your pinkies toward the sky" to maximize triceps engagement

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IgSjoXbpy1M&t=2

exercises.name: FlexBar Wrist Flexion
exercises.description: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing up and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist extend back, then curl the wrist up to raise the bar while the forearm stays still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. Works the wrist flexors, and is the companion movement to FlexBar wrist extension for balanced forearm strengthening.

exercises.name: knee push-ups
exercises.description:
1. Start by kneeling on the floor, keeping your knees together. Place your hands on the floor in front of you, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
  2. Make sure your body forms a straight line from head to knees. Hands should be positioned below shoulders.
  3. Lower your torso towards the ground, bending your elbows while keeping your trunk stable. Keep your knees in contact with the floor.
  4. Push through your hands to return to the starting position. Be sure to maintain contraction of chest, shoulder and arm muscles at the top of the movement.
  5. Perform the desired number of repetitions, controlling the movement and maintaining good form.

exercises.name: Renegade Row
exercises.description:
Get into pushup position gripping some dumbbells. Perform one pushup, then drive your left elbo up, bringing the dumbell up to your body. Return the dumbell to starting position.

Perform another pushup and then row with the other arm to complete one rep.

exercises.name: Supine press
exercises.description: Take a close grip and push perpendicular to the bench. Keep back flat.

exercises.name: Wrist curl, dumbbells
exercises.description:
1. Sitting on a bench, grab the dumbbell with your palms facing up and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees.
  2. Perform the movement by curling your palms and wrists towards your face.
  3. (optional/variable) Pause at the top.
  4. Slowly return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Limber 11
exercises.description:
Limber 11
Source: Joe DeFranco

1. Foam Roll IT Band [soft_tissue] - 10-15 passes
2. Foam Roll Adductors [soft_tissue] - 10-15 passes
3. SMR Glutes (lax ball) [soft_tissue] - 30 sec-2 min
4. Bent-knee Iron Cross [dynamic] - 5-10 reps each side
5. Roll-overs into V-sits [dynamic] - 10 reps
6. Rocking Frog Stretch [dynamic] - 10 reps
7. Fire Hydrant Circles [dynamic] - 10 forward / 10 backward
8. Mountain Climbers [dynamic] - 10 reps each leg
9. Cossack Squats [dynamic] - 5-10 reps each side
10. Seated Piriformis Stretch [isometric] - 20-30 sec each side
11. Rear-foot-elevated Hip Flexor Stretch [dynamic + 3s hold] - 5-10 reps each side

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
exercises.description: The reverse-grip barbell curl is a variation on the biceps curl where the palms face downward. The switch from an underhand to an overhand grip brings the forearm and brachialis muscles more into the exercise.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise Isometric
exercises.description: An isometric lateral raise is a shoulder exercise where you hold your arms out to the sides at waist height for a set amount of time instead of moving up and down

exercises.name: Isometric Wrist Curl Hold
exercises.description: Sit on a bench with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing up, holding a dumbbell or barbell. Curl the wrist all the way up and hold the top position for the set time, squeezing hard. This builds cupping strength and tendon resilience for grip and arm wrestling. Do it straight after your wrist curls without changing seats.

exercises.name: Unilateral Lunges
exercises.description: No stops during movement, hands on the hips.

exercises.name: Walking
exercises.description: Walking outdoor or indoor, try keeping a pace of at list 100 steps per minute.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: DL from top to pos 2: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WtWtjViRsKo

exercises.name: Legend Chest Press
exercises.description: Plate-loaded chest press machine from Legend Fitness LeverEdge line.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: The Wall Angels exercise primarily targets the upper back and shoulder muscles, helping improve posture, shoulder mobility, and scapular control.

exercises.name: Left neck stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Sit or stand with your back straight.

Steps:

  1. Tilt your head to the side.
  2. Take the hand closer to your head and use it to grab your head from the other side.
  3. Push with your hand against your head and with your head against your hand so that the forces balance out and your head stays still.
  4. Maintain this tension until the end of the exercise.

exercises.name: Shoulder External Rotation with Dumbbell
exercises.description:
1. Lie on your side holding a dumbbell in your upper hand
  2. Tuck your elbow into your side and rest the hand in front of you
  3. Rotate the shoulder so the hand raises up
  4. Lower the hand down

exercises.name: Bent Over Rowing Reverse
exercises.description:
The same as regular rowing, but holding a reversed grip (your palms pointing forwards):

Grab the barbell with a wide grIp (slightly more than shoulder wide) and lean forward. Your upper body is not quite parallel to the floor, but forms a slight angle. The chest's out during the whole exercise.

Pull now the barbell with a fast movement towards your belly button, not further up. Go slowly down to the initial position. Don't swing with your body and keep your arms next to your body.

exercises.name: Step Jack
exercises.description:
The Step Jack is a low-impact plyometric-style move that provides cardiovascular benefits without the joint stress of jumping. It works the entire body, specifically targeting the legs, core, and shoulders. This move is ideal for beginners, individuals with joint sensitivities, or as a dynamic warm-up to gradually elevate the heart rate. Notes (Instructions):

  1. ​Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides.
  2. ​Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously swinging both arms up above your head.
  3. Bring your right foot back to the center and lower your arms.
  4. ​Immediately repeat the movement, stepping out with your left foot.
  5. ​Continue alternating sides at a steady, rhythmic pace.

exercises.name: Rear-foot-elevated Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description:
Rear-foot-elevated Hip Flexor Stretch
Part of: Limber 11
Source: Joe DeFranco
Prescription: 5-10 reps each side
Type: dynamic
Includes dynamic movement plus 3s hold.

exercises.name: Isometric Wipers
exercises.description:
Assume push-up position, with hands slightly wider than shoulder width.

Shift body weight as far as possible to one side, allowing the elbow on that side to flex.

Reverse the motion, moving completely over to the other side.

Return to the starting position, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Straight-arm Pull Down (rope Attachment)
exercises.description: Use the rope attachment on a high pulley. Grasp the two ends of the rope with your arms straight out in front of you. Pull your hands down towards your hips, while keeping your arms straight, then raise them back up to the starting position.

exercises.name: Side Crunch
exercises.description: Hold weight in one hand. Bend side ways to the knee. Pull upo to upright position using your obliquus.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
• Starting Position: Lie on your back (supine) on a mat, with your legs extended and relaxed. Arms can be placed alongside your body or out to the sides for stability.
  • The Movement: Slightly lift one leg off the floor (keeping it straight or with a slight bend). Move it laterally outward, away from the other leg, as if stepping over a small obstacle.
  • Range of Motion: Move the leg as far as comfortable without lifting your pelvis or rotating your torso, feeling a stretch in the inner thigh and hip.
  • Return: Slowly bring the leg back to the starting position with controlled movement.
  • Goal: Improves lateral hip mobility (abduction) and strengthens the pelvic stabilizer muscles.

exercises.name: Elevated prayer stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position: Kneel in front of a bench, far enough so that your torso can fit between your knees and the bench. With your back straight, place your elbows on the bench, with palms together, hands pointing up. Steps:

  1. On exhale, stretch your chest down toward the floor without moving your lower back. At the same time, bring your hands toward your shoulders, keeping palms together and elbows on the bench.
  2. Hold for a few seconds.
  3. On inhale, relax your back to return to the starting position.
    1. Repeat.

exercises.name: Band Terminal Knee extension
exercises.description: This is an end range strengthening exercise for the knee extensors. Start by looping a band around the back of one knee and anchoring the other end to a stable surface in front of you. Stand in a split stance with the banded knee bent and placed as the front leg. Straighten the knee to pull against the bands resistance and maintain a contraction in your quadriceps for up to 5 seconds before releasing.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.description: Starting on back, move to the standing position with dumbbell in one hand.  Switch hands between reps.

exercises.name: Squat Thrust
exercises.description: The burpee, or squat thrust, is a full body exercise used in strength training and as an aerobic exercise. The basic movement is performed in four steps and known as a four-count burpee: Begin in a standing position. Move into a squat position with your hands on the ground. (count 1) Kick your feet back into a plank position, while keeping your arms extended. (count 2) Immediately return your feet into squat position. (count 3) Stand up from the squat position (count 4)

exercises.name: Bent Over Row
exercises.description: Standing with the torso bent forward from the hips at roughly 45 degrees, back straight. Hold two dumbbells with an overhand grip, arms hanging below the shoulders. Pull the dumbbells along the body toward the pelvis, elbows close to the torso, briefly squeezing the shoulder blades together at the top. Lower under control. Primary muscle: lats. Keep the torso stable throughout the movement, no arching of the lower back.

exercises.name: Triceps Extensions on Cable
exercises.description: Grab the cable, stand with your feet shoulder wide, keep your back straight and lean forward a little. Push the bar down, making sure the elbows don't move during the exercise. Rotate your hands outwards at the very end and go back to the initial position without pause.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Cheat Curl
exercises.description:
1. Starting position is standing with feet shoulder width apart.
  2. Hands should take an underhand or supinated grip on the dumbbells holding them with hands shoulder width apart.
  3. Keeping elbows tucked into your sides throughout the entire movement, use momentum to curl the dumbbells, squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
  4. Slowly lower to return to the starting position. Keep the core tight throughout the exercise.

Cheating through the concentric curling portion of this challenging exercise gives us a great opportunity to increase time under tension and create eccentric overload with heavier weight when we lower.

exercises.name: Fat Grip Dumbbell Hold
exercises.description: Fit thick grip sleeves over two dumbbell handles, or wrap the handles in a towel to make them thicker. Stand tall holding one in each hand at your sides and hold for the set time without letting the handles roll in your hands. The thicker handle makes your fingers and thumb work much harder than a normal grip.

exercises.name: Lunges
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Stand with back straight.

Steps:

  1. Take a large step forward with your left leg.
  2. Bring your pelvis down until you almost touch the floor with your right knee.
  3. Bring your pelvis back up.
  4. Return to the starting position by stepping back.
  5. Repeat, switching legs each time.

exercises.name: High Knee Skips HD
exercises.description: You can use this exercise both as a dynamic warm-up before training and add it to your cardio training routine to burn fat. High knee skips are a plyometric exercise. Plyometrics are explosive aerobic moves that increase speed, quickness, and power and they work your whole body. High knee skips target the oblique, leg muscles, hip muscles and hip flexors and also work on the thighs, knee tendons, quadriceps and shoulders. Jumps are beneficial to your health because they combine cardiovascular conditioning with strength work. Since jumps elevate your heart rate, they can also improve your cardiovascular fitness.

exercises.name: Kong Curl
exercises.description: This exercise is somewhat similar to a cable curl and a cable crossover. But instead of a chest/biceps exercise, this exercise targets the brachialis muscle, responsible for that broad arm when viewed from a front view. During the exercise, maintain a pronated forearm position with starting position of approx. 45 degree pronated. Start with slightly bend elbows and alternately curl until your hands (your thumb first) meet your upper middle chest (similar to how Kong hits his chest, thus the name of this exercise).

exercises.name: FlexBar Tyler Twist
exercises.description: An eccentric exercise for the wrist extensors, done with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar, and widely used in rehabilitation for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). Hold the bar vertically in the affected hand with the wrist extended. Grasp the top of the bar with the other hand, palm facing away, and twist the top hand to wind up the bar. Bring both arms out in front of you with the bar horizontal, then slowly let the affected wrist untwist the bar over about four seconds while the other hand holds steady. Reset and repeat. The reverse version, twisting in the opposite direction for the wrist flexors, is used for medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow). Move slowly and stop if the exercise causes sharp pain rather than the expected mild discomfort.

exercises.name: Rowing, T-bar
exercises.description:
The execution of this exercise is very similar to the regular bent over rowing, only that the bar is fixed here.

Grab the barbell with a wide grip (slightly more than shoulder wide) and lean forward. Your upper body is not quite parallel to the floor, but forms a slight angle. The chest's out during the whole exercise. Pull now the barbell with a fast movement towards your belly button, not further up. Go slowly down to the initial position. Don't swing with your body and keep your arms next to your body.

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.description:
1. Load the sled with 25% of your maximum load. If you don’t know this, choose a weight you can push for 10 minutes with short breaks. Beginners may choose to push the sled with no weight.
  2. Stand behind the sled and grab the poles with a high-grip hand position.
  3. Engage your core muscles and start pushing the sled forward as fast as you can, powering through your entire leg. Extend your hips and knees as you move the sled forward. Your foot stance should resemble your natural running position.

exercises.name: Head turns
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Sit or stand with your back straight and shoulders down.

Steps:

  1. Sit or stand up straight, shoulders dropped.
  2. Turn your head to the side as far as possible. Stop when you hit a barrier and hold for 5 seconds.
  3. Return to center position and repeat, changing sides.

exercises.name: Toe Taps
exercises.description: Toe taps are a core-focused exercise performed lying on your back. Lie flat with your arms by your sides and your legs raised to a tabletop position (knees bent at 90 degrees). Slowly lower one foot to gently tap the floor, keeping your core engaged and your lower back pressed into the ground. Return to the starting position and alternate legs. This exercise strengthens the core while minimizing strain on the lower back.

exercises.name: Dumbbell farmer's carry
exercises.description: Grab half your body weight in each hand and walk.

exercises.name: Solo Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: See this instructive video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qHwyBHS6MQs .

exercises.name: Medicine ball booklet crunch
exercises.description: Using a medicine ball as an overload will make the exercise heavier.

exercises.name: Elephant Walks
exercises.description: Hinge at your hips until you feel a stretch behind your knees. Bend one leg while the other is straight then fluidly bend the other knee while straightening the first knee.

exercises.name: Handstand
exercises.description: Handstand free standing by pressing arms into the ground and contracting core and glutes

exercises.name: Crunches With Cable (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Crunches With Cable with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: TRX/Rings Push-Up
exercises.description:
1. Set TRX straps or rings so the handles hang just above the floor, or at a height that allows a full push-up range with your feet on the ground.
  2. Grip one handle or ring in each hand. Get into a plank with the body in one straight line from head to heels, arms extended, and the straps vertical under the shoulders.
  3. Brace the core and glutes. Keep the wrists neutral and the shoulders packed down away from the ears.
  4. Bend the elbows and lower the chest between the hands until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor or you reach a comfortable depth.
  5. Keep the elbows at roughly 45 degrees from the torso; do not flare them fully out to the sides.
  6. Press through the hands to extend the arms and return to the plank. Exhale on the way up, pause briefly at the top with control, and repeat.

On rings, keep the rings close to the body so they do not drift wide. Difficulty increases if the feet are elevated or the straps are set lower so the body is more horizontal; a higher handle position makes it easier.

exercises.name: Straight Bar Cable Curls
exercises.description: Standing upright in front of Cable Tower using a straight bar

exercises.name: Horse Stance (Side Splits)
exercises.description:
1. Stand as for a squat, with your feet wide and your toes pointed slightly outwards.
  2. Gently squat into a deep, wide squat - your hips should be below your knees.
  3. Hold for 3 to 5 seconds.
  4. Come up under control, and repeat as needed.

exercises.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rows (Two Arms)
exercises.description:
How to Perform It

  • Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral or overhand grip.
  • Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back, until your torso is roughly 45–75 degrees to the floor. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
  • Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders with arms fully extended.
  • Keep your back flat, chest up, and core braced — avoid rounding your spine.
  • Pull the dumbbells up toward your ribcage/hips, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
  • Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
  • Lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position.
  • Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Key Coaching Cues

  • Hinge from the hips, not the lower back
  • Keep the spine neutral throughout — no rounding
  • Lead with the elbows, not the hands
  • Avoid using momentum or jerking the weight up
  • Control the eccentric (lowering) phase rather than letting the weights drop

exercises.name: FlexBar Wrist Extension
exercises.description: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing down and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist drop, then extend the wrist to raise the bar, keeping the forearm still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. The resistance comes from twisting or bending the flexible bar, so a thicker or stiffer bar increases the load. Commonly used for wrist and forearm strengthening and for elbow tendon rehabilitation.

exercises.description:
Exercises for strengthening knee and leg musculature.
