exercises.name: Vpushup
exercises.description: Lift your body off the ground by pushing your arms upwards

exercises.name: Head tilts
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Sit or stand with your back straight.

Steps:

  1. Tilt your head to one side and hold for a bit.
  2. Return your head to neutral position and hold for a bit.
  3. Tilt your head to the other side and hold for a bit.
  4. Return your head to neutral position yet again and hold for a bit.
  5. Repeat.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.description:
Lay down on a bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.

If you train with a high weight it is advisable to have a spotter that can help you up if you can't lift the weight on your own.

With the width of the grip you can also control which part of the chest is trained more:

  • wide grip: outer chest muscles
  • narrow grip: inner chest muscles and triceps

exercises.name: Seated Knee Tuck
exercises.description: Sit on floor or mat. Place arms slightly behind you. Raise legs. Now extend your legs and pull them back.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Cable Y-Raise
exercises.description: Attach a D-Bar to the cable machine. Perform a motion akin to drawing a sword from across your body.

exercises.name: Weighted push-ups
exercises.description:
• Setup: Begin in a standard plank position with a weight plate balanced securely on your upper back.
  • Alignment: Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels, engaging your core to prevent your back from sagging.
  • Execution: Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your elbows at a forty-five degrees.
  • Ascent: Press through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions
exercises.description: Lie on the hyperextension pillow with your navel at the front edge, allowing your upper body to hang freely. Tighten all your back muscles and raise your torso until you're horizontal, but no higher. Lower yourself slowly, maintaining a steady flow of muscles.

exercises.name: Reverse Cable Flye
exercises.description: Attach D-Handles to two cable pulleys in the upper position. Grab the left on with your right hand and vice-versa.

exercises.name: Pike Push Ups
exercises.description: Push Up performed from a pike position (optional to have feet elevated).

exercises.name: Leg Curls (laying)
exercises.description: Lay on a bench and put your calves behind the leg holder (better if they are hold on around the lower calves). Hold a grip on the bars to make sure the body is firmly in place. Bend your legs bringing the weight up, go slowly back. During the exercise the body should not move, all work is done by the legs.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Underhand)
exercises.description:
Execution

  1. Starting position:

    • Hold the barbell with arms fully extended toward the floor.
    • Maintain tension in your lats and back muscles.

exercises.name: Extreme Pec Stretch
exercises.description: Deep loaded stretch for pectorals, typically performed at end of chest work.

exercises.name: Neutral Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Lat pull downs with a neutral grip on the bar.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.description: The machine lateral raise is an isolation exercise that targets the medial (side) deltoid muscle to build wider, more defined shoulders. The machine's fixed path of motion provides greater stability than dumbbells, making it ideal for beginners or those who want to focus solely on muscle activation.

exercises.name: Bus Drivers
exercises.description: Sitting with a Weight Plate, used as wheel, in both hands; raised slightly below eye level

exercises.name: Bench Press Narrow Grip
exercises.description:
• Setup: Lie flat on the bench and grip the bar at shoulder-width (closer than a standard bench press).
  • Descent: Lower the bar with control to your lower chest.
  • Form: Keep your elbows tucked in tight against your torso—do not let them flare out.
  • Ascent: Press the bar straight back up, squeezing your triceps at the top.

exercises.name: Triceps Dips (Assisted)
exercises.description: Assisted triceps dips  is a gym work out exercise that targets triceps and also involves chest.

exercises.name: Curl with kettlebell two hands
exercises.description: Stand upright and grip the kettlebell with both hands. Perform the elbow flexion motion, starting from a fully extended position until your hand reaches shoulder height. Spread your legs a little for stability and, to perform the exercise correctly, try not to push with your back or body in general. Change the weight of the kettlebell to adjust the difficulty.

exercises.name: Tuck planche
exercises.description: Basic calisthenics progression for the full planche

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and bending sideways to work the oblique muscles on the side of the body. It can be done standing or seated and is often used as a core strengthening exercise.

exercises.name: High Knee Jumps
exercises.description:
• Start with legs slightly wider than shoulder width
  • Drop into a bodyweight squat
  • As you hit the bottom of the squat, explode upwards into a jump while simultaneously tucking your knees into your chest midflight.  Remain tucked until the apex of your jump.
  • Land on both feet, making sure your knees are not locked so as to avoid excessive strain upon your joints.  Collect yourself into the next rep as quickly but under control as possible.

exercises.name: Wall-sit
exercises.description: The Wall Sit (or wall chair) is an isometric exercise that mainly involves the leg muscles, improving muscular endurance and stability. Here are the main and secondary muscles activated during the exercise.

exercises.name: Treadmill Cardio
exercises.description:
It's a cardiovascular workout performed on a treadmill to improve endurance, burn calories, and promote heart health. It offers multiple benefits, such as the ability to easily adjust speed and incline, allowing for a variety of workouts, from hill walking to high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and tempo runs. To optimize results, it's important to vary your workouts. Benefits of Treadmill Cardio:

  • Improved Cardiovascular Health: Regular aerobic exercise on a treadmill strengthens the heart and lungs, which can help prevent heart disease.
  • Weight Loss: By burning calories, treadmill training can be an effective tool for weight loss and maintaining a healthy weight.
  • Muscle Strengthening: It strengthens the muscles in the legs and glutes, helping to prevent muscle loss, which is especially important with age.
  • Training Flexibility: Allows you to vary speed, incline, and intervals, making your workout more dynamic and adaptable to different fitness levels. Types of Treadmill Training:
  • Hill Walking: Increasing the incline of the treadmill and walking at a brisk pace can improve endurance and work your leg muscles.
  • Endurance Jog: A run at a comfortable, steady pace that keeps your heart rate in a target zone (such as Zone 2) to build endurance.
  • Interval Training: Alternating periods of high intensity (fast running) with periods of low intensity (easy walking or jogging) to maximize calorie burn and cardiovascular improvement.
  • Tempo Run: A run at a steady, sustained pace that is slightly faster than a normal jog, which challenges your ability to sustain a more intense effort for an extended period.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Raises
exercises.description: Seated on a bench with the dumbbells on the floor bend over at 45 Degrees and then slowly raise each dumbbell to shoulder height and hold for a couple seconds before lowering to the starting position.

exercises.name: Crunches on Machine
exercises.description: The procedure is very similar as for regular crunches, only with the additional weight of the machine. Sit on the machine, put both feet firmly on the ground. Grab the to the weights, cables, etc. and do a rolling motion forwards (the spine should ideally lose touch vertebra by vertebra). Slowly return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Australian pull-ups
exercises.description:
1. Lie down under a high bar or suspension bar, positioned at an appropriate height.
  2. Position yourself on your back under the bar, gripping the bar with a supinated grip (palms facing you).
  3. Adjust your position so that your body is aligned straight from head to toe. Arms should be fully extended, shoulders stabilized, and legs aligned with the rest of the body.
  4. Bend your elbows and pull your chest towards the bar, contracting your back muscles. Imagine you're trying to bring your shoulder blades together.
  5. Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a moment to maximize muscle activation.
  6. Slowly return to the starting position, extending your elbows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Squat
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and performing a squat while stepping to the side. It targets the legs, glutes, and core muscles.

exercises.name: Trap press
exercises.description: Laying flat with arm pointing straight upwards, elbow fully extended, use only your shoulder to raise the weight as high as comfortable and back to rest.

exercises.name: Machine Incline Chest Press (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Machine Incline Chest Press with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: rubber band glute kickback
exercises.description: A rubber band glute kickback is an exercise performed on hands and knees, where you anchor a resistance band to your foot and kick your heel back and up, squeezing your glute at the top of the movement, while maintaining a stable core and flat back to target and strengthen the gluteal muscles.

exercises.name: Biceps Curls With SZ-bar
exercises.description:
Hold the SZ-bar shoulder-wide, the back is straight, the shoulders slightly back, the arms are streched. Bend the arms, bringing the weight up, with a fast movement. Without pausing, let down the bar with a slow and controlled movement.

Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).

exercises.name: Wrist Roller
exercises.description: Hold a wrist roller, a short bar with a rope and a small weight attached, with both hands at shoulder height and arms straight out in front. Roll the bar with your wrists to wind the rope up until the weight reaches the bar, then unwind it slowly. Roll forward and backward on different sets to train both sides of the forearm.

exercises.name: Talons fesses
exercises.description: Touch your heels to your buttocks, while remaining static or moving

exercises.name: Dumbbell close grip bench press
exercises.description: Lie down with your back on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Raise your arms towards the ceiling with your palms facing each other and dumbbells pressed together. Slowly lower the dumbbells to your chest, then slowly push them back. Repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: Push Press
exercises.description: Clean your dumbbells onto your shoulders, palms facing in. Take a breath and brace your core. (picture 1)Dip at the knees and use your legs to help (picture 2) press your dumbbells overhead. Lower under control with a slow tempo to your shoulders and repeat.

exercises.name: Toes to bar
exercises.description: The name "Toes to Bar" says it all: This exercise, in which you hang from a pull-up bar, involves bringing your toes toward the bar, pointing toward your face. This really works your abdominal muscles. "Toes to Bar" is popular in functional fitness programs like Freeletics and CrossFit, and is an effective exercise for six-pack training.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
exercises.description:
• Setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 45 to 60 degrees.
  • Starting Position: Sit back against the bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor with your palms facing forward (supinated grip).
  • The Curl: Keeping your upper arms stationary and shoulders pinned back against the bench, exhale and curl the weights upward toward your shoulders.
  • Peak Contraction: Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows do not swing forward.
  • The Descent: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining full control and feeling the stretch in the biceps.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
exercises.description: Single leg squat where one leg is behind you.

exercises.name: Reverse Fly Standing
exercises.description:
1. Stand with a good posture holding a cable in each hand opposite the machine
  2. Starting with the hands in front of your chest pull the arms out to your side into the shape of a T with the elbows nearly straight
  3. Slowly release the arms forward to the start
  4. Repeat with the arms moving into the shape of a Y
  5. Repeat with the arms in the shape of a W
  6. Repeat with the arms in the shape of an L by your side

exercises.name: Single-Arm Backpack Row
exercises.description: Stand with your feet staggered and bend forward at the hips, keeping your back neutral. Hold a securely closed, weighted backpack by a strong handle with one hand. Support your free hand on your thigh for stability. Pull the backpack towards your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body. Slowly lower the backpack to the starting position without rotating your torso. Complete all repetitions before switching arms.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squats right
exercises.description:
1. Stand tall in front of a chair and take a large step. Put the upper part of one of your feet on the chair.
  2. Bend the front knee, balancing with arms until the back knee almost touches the ground.
  3. Push back to the starting position and repeat.

exercises.name: Close-grip Press-ups
exercises.description: Drop into a strong plank position, bringing your hands close together until they're almost touching. (picture 1)Bend your elbows to slowly bring your chest to the floor (picture 2). Keep your elbows close to your body as you push back up explosively. Repeat. Ensure you take your time lowering on each rep, keeping your form sharp.

exercises.name: Alternating High Cable Row
exercises.description:
1. Start by putting the attachment in a high position on the cable station and step back about 1m from the attachment. Grab the cable pulley handle in your left hand at about head height with your elbow slightly bent. Step back with your left foot.
  2. Pull your elbow joint in toward the torso twisting slightly and perform a single-arm row. Engage the lats as you twist.
  3. Return to the starting position with cable pulley and left foot and grab the cable pulley handle in the right hand. Repeat this motion on the opposite side with your right foot stepped back.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.description:
Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides and feet hip-width apart. For a larger range of motion, stand with the balls of your feet on a step or a weight plate.

Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and pause briefly at the top. Then lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves. Keep your knees straight but not locked and your upper body upright.

exercises.name: Single Leg Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description:
Sit on the floor with one leg extended straight in front of you, toes pointing up. Bend the other leg and rest the sole of that foot against the inner thigh of the straight leg, letting the knee fall out to the side.

Sit up tall with your chest open and your shoulders back. Breathe in, then as you breathe out, lean forward from the hips over the straight leg while keeping your back long. Reach for your shin, ankle or foot, only as far as you can without rounding your back, and hold. Then switch sides.

exercises.name: Dynamic side hold
exercises.description: Sling a rubber band on a kettlebell and lift the kettlebell by the rubber band. Let it hang by your side and stand on one leg, switch leg while continuing hold. Repeat with other hand

exercises.name: Lateral Push Off
exercises.description: Push off the ground and land on one leg and regain balance before jumping to the other leg

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Squat
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height and performing a squat. It targets the lower body muscles, including the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core and upper body.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.description: Belly breathing. Hand on chest stays still, hand on belly rises. 8-10 slow breaths.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform the Bulgarian split squat with an upright torso, rear foot on a bench, lower until the front thigh is parallel, keep the knee over the toes, hold a rack for balance if needed.

exercises.name: Wall Squat
exercises.description:
Find a nice flat piece of wall and stand with your back leaning against the wall. Slowly slide down the wall while moving your feet away from it, until your thighs are parallel to the ground and both your knees and your hips are bent at a 90° angle. Cross your arms in front of your chest and hold this position for 30 seconds.

Variant: put a big inflated rubber ball (like a small basketball) between your knees and squeeze the ball while holding the squat position

exercises.name: Hindu Pushups
exercises.description: Exercise to strengthen the shoulders and pectorals. Its name is due to the fact that it begins in the Yoga position "Dog Facing Down", passing to "Cobra" but without resting the legs or torso on the ground to finally end with a normal flexion. The exercise can also be performed backwards (back to the starting position). As a variation, after doing the push-up, the hip can be raised to return to downward facing dog.

exercises.name: High-Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Stand next to a cable machine with the pulley set to waist height.

Grab the opposite-side handle with the hand farthest from the pulley, keeping your palm facing in.

Keep your core engaged, chest lifted, and shoulders relaxed. Maintain a slight bend in the elbow throughout the lift.

Lift your arm out to the side until your elbow reaches shoulder height, keeping your wrist aligned with your elbow.

Briefly pause at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to your side with control. Repeat for the desired reps.

exercises.name: Leg Curl
exercises.description: The leg curl, also known as the hamstring curl, is an isolation exercise that targets the hamstring muscles. The exercise involves flexing the lower leg against resistance towards the buttocks. Other exercises that can be used to strengthen the hamstrings are the glute-ham raise and the deadlift.

exercises.name: Butchers Block Stretch
exercises.description:
1. Kneel down with the hands together
  2. Rest the elbows on a bench in front of you and lower the chest down
  3. Keep the elbows bent with good posture and hold

exercises.name: Burpees

exercises.name: Extreme Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description: Deep loaded stretch for deltoids, performed after pressing movements.

exercises.name: Knee to Chest Stretch
exercises.description: The knee to chest stretch is a simple yet effective exercise for relieving lower back tension and improving hip mobility. To perform, lie flat on your back with your legs extended. Bring one knee toward your chest, wrapping your hands around your shin or behind your thigh. Gently pull the knee closer to your chest while keeping the other leg straight on the floor. Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds, then switch sides. For a deeper stretch, both knees can be pulled toward the chest simultaneously.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch Hold
exercises.description: The plate pinch hold is a grip strength exercise designed to target the forearms and improve grip endurance. Select one or two weight plates (smooth-edged plates work best) and pinch them together between your thumb and fingers. Hold the plates with your arm straight down by your side or extended slightly in front of you. Maintain the hold for as long as you can, keeping your shoulders relaxed and your grip firm. This exercise can be done for time or repetitions.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press, on Machine (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Shoulder Press, on Machine with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: TRX/Rings Dip
exercises.description:
1. Set TRX straps or rings so the handles hang at a height that lets you support your body with straight arms and the feet clear of the floor, or lightly assisted if needed.
  2. Grip one handle or ring in each hand. Jump or step into a support hold: arms locked out, shoulders packed down, chest up, and the body tight from head to heels. On rings, turn the palms slightly inward (rings turned out) for a stable lockout.
  3. Brace the core and lean the torso slightly forward.
  4. Bend the elbows and lower under control until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or to a depth you can reverse without shoulder pain. Keep the elbows close to the body rather than flaring wide.
  5. On rings, keep the rings close to the sides so they do not drift outward.
  6. Press through the hands to extend the arms and return to the support hold. Exhale on the way up, pause briefly at the top with full lockout, and repeat.

Assisted variations: keep the feet on the floor or a box and use the legs lightly. Harder variations: slower eccentrics, pauses at the bottom, or a more forward lean for more chest emphasis.

exercises.name: Push-Ups | Incline
exercises.description: Inclined push-ups primarily target the chest muscles (pectoralis major and minor), but also work the triceps, shoulders, and core to a lesser extent. Because the upper body is elevated, the incline push-up places less emphasis on the triceps compared to regular push-ups, which may be beneficial for individuals looking to specifically target their chest muscles.

exercises.name: Bent Over Rowing
exercises.description:
1. Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
  2. Now, while keeping the torso stationary, breathe out and lift the barbell to you. Keep the elbows close to the body and only use the forearms to hold the weight. At the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a brief pause.
  3. Then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
  4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Curl De Muñeca Con Barra
exercises.description:
This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.

  1. Starting Position: Grip a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing up) at a width similar to your shoulders.

  2. Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion.

  3. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch.

  4. Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second.

  5. Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.

exercises.name: Row
exercises.description: In strength training, rowing (or a row, usually preceded by a qualifying adjective — for instance a seated row) is an exercise where the purpose is to strengthen the muscles that draw the rower's arms toward the body (latissimus dorsi) as well as those that retract the scapulae (trapezius and rhomboids) and those that support the spine (erector spinae). When done on a rowing machine, rowing also exercises muscles that extend and support the legs (quadriceps and thigh muscles). In all cases, the abdominal and lower back muscles must be used in order to support the body and prevent back injury.

Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs.

exercises.name: Push-Ups | Decline
exercises.description: Decline push-ups are another modified version of the traditional push-up that target the upper body muscles in a different way. To perform a decline push-up, elevate your feet on an elevated surface, such as a bench, chair, or step, while placing your hands on the ground in a push-up position. Lower your body towards the ground while maintaining a straight line from your shoulders to your ankles, and then push back up to the starting position. Unlike the inclined push-up, the decline push-up places more emphasis on the shoulders and triceps, while still engaging the chest muscles to a lesser extent. By elevating your feet, you increase the difficulty of the exercise by placing more weight on your upper body, forcing your shoulders and triceps to work harder to push your body back up. The decline push-up can be a great way to challenge your upper body strength and improve your ability to perform other push-up variations. As with any exercise, be sure to use proper form and start with a height that is appropriate for your strength and fitness level.

exercises.name: dumbbell snatch
exercises.description:
Key Steps to Execute Correctly:

Setup: Place the dumbbell between your feet, with your shoulders above your hips, chest up, and back flat.

The Pull: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) to drive the dumbbell upward, keeping your elbow high and the dumbbell close to your body.

The Catch: Quickly flex your hips and knees to drop under the dumbbell and receive it overhead with your arm locked in position, landing in a half-squat stance.

Common Mistakes: Using your arms too much to lift the weight instead of your legs, having a low elbow during the pull phase, and misaligning your shoulder, elbow, and wrist in the final position. For beginners, it’s recommended to start with light loads, focus on technique, and perform 3 to 5 sets of 3 to 5 reps per arm.

exercises.name: Single-leg BOSU balance
exercises.description:
Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise

The exercise for balancing on a BOSU ball while standing on one leg is known as the single-leg BOSU balance exercise. This exercise is effective for enhancing balance, coordination, and core stability.

Benefits of the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
  • Improves Balance: Standing on one leg challenges your stability.
  • Enhances Coordination: Engaging different muscle groups helps improve overall coordination.
  • Strengthens Core: The exercise activates core muscles, promoting better posture and stability.
How to Perform the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
  1. Positioning: Stand on the dome side of the BOSU ball with one leg.
  2. Balance: Keep your opposite leg lifted and your core engaged.
  3. Duration: Aim to hold the position for 10-20 seconds, gradually increasing the time as you improve.
Progression Tips
  • Add Movement: Try reaching for objects around you while maintaining balance.
  • Close Your Eyes: This increases the challenge by removing visual stability cues.
  • Use a Ball: Catch or toss a ball while balancing to further engage your core and coordination.

This exercise is a great way to build foundational balance skills before progressing to more complex movements.

exercises.name: Kegel Exercise

Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit upright in a chair. Locate the pelvic floor muscles: they are the muscles you would use to stop the flow of urine or to hold back gas. Keep your abdomen, glutes and thighs relaxed and breathe normally throughout.

Tighten the pelvic floor muscles and lift them gently upwards and inwards. Hold the contraction for a few seconds, then release completely and rest for at least as long as you held. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

The exercise can be varied by holding longer with a light contraction (endurance) or by performing quick, short contractions with a full relaxation in between.

exercises.name: Archer Pull Up
exercises.description:
An archer pull-up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that strengthens your back and biceps, serving as a progression towards a one-arm pull-up. It gets its name from the "bow-drawing" position your body takes at the top.Here's how to do it:

  1. Grip: Grasp a pull-up bar with a wider-than-shoulder-width overhand grip.
  2. Starting Position: Hang with arms fully extended, engaging your core and keeping your shoulder blades pulled down.
  3. The Pull: Pull your body up towards one hand, similar to a regular pull-up. At the same time, extend the other arm out to the side, keeping it as straight as possible. Your chin should come towards the hand that is pulling.
  4. Hold & Lower: Briefly hold the top position where one arm is bent and pulling, and the other is extended. Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
  5. Alternate: Repeat the movement, pulling up towards the opposite hand.The key to this exercise is to keep the assisting arm as straight as possible to maximise the load on the working arm. This makes it a challenging but effective exercise for unilateral pulling strength.

exercises.name: Torso Twist
exercises.description: Standing Torso Twist WorkoutTarget your core and improve flexibility with this dynamic standing exercise! The Standing Torso Twist Workout involves twisting your torso while keeping your feet and hips stable, engaging your obliques, and stretching your entire upper body. This movement helps to:Strengthen core musclesIncrease flexibility in the spine and torsoImprove posture and balanceEnhance overall athletic performancePerform 3 sets of 10-15 reps, twisting to each side, to feel the benefits of this effective and efficient workout!

exercises.name: Behind the Back Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Lateral raises have long been a staple for building capped delts, and lifters use everything from dumbbells and bands to machines and single-arm variations to make them grow.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Stretch
exercises.description: Extend your right arm straight across your chest toward the left. Hook your left arm around your right elbow and pull your right arm a little closer to your body. Keep your shoulder down as you do this. Repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Lateral Rows on Cable, One Armed
exercises.description: Set cable at waist height, start with arm across your belly and move han over and out too other side, one arm at the time.

exercises.name: Kick with Board
exercises.description: Hold a kickboard with both hands, arms extended in front of you, face in the water (lift head forward to breathe when needed). Kick from your hips, not your knees, keeping your legs mostly straight with a slight bend and a steady, compact flutter kick. This builds leg endurance and keeps your body horizontal without needing to worry about your arms.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press - Dumbbell
exercises.description:
This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.

  1. Bench Adjustment and Preparation: Set the bench to an incline of between 30 and 45 degrees (an incline greater than 45° will place too much strain on the shoulders and reduce the stimulus to the chest). Sit down with a dumbbell on each thigh.

  2. Starting position: Lean back, resting your back against the bench, while using your knees one after the other to push the dumbbells upward to shoulder height.

  3. Anatomical Stabilization: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your scapulas (bring your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench) to protect your shoulders and stabilize the load.

  4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells slowly and in a controlled manner toward the upper part of your chest. Your elbows should not splay out to the sides (90°); maintain a safe angle of about 45 to 60 degrees relative to your torso.

  5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the dumbbells vertically upward as you exhale. Follow a slightly converging path (without letting them touch at the top). Stop the movement just before locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension in the upper pectoral.

exercises.name: Standing Leg Lift with External Rotation (Custom)
exercises.description: Stand and lift one bent knee out to the side with external rotation, move slowly under control, ten reps per side, hold a wall for balance if needed, keep the torso upright.

exercises.name: Alternate back lunges
exercises.description: The posterior muscles of the buttocks, hamstrings, soleus and gastrocnemius are trained more

exercises.name: Modified pulldown
exercises.description: With an inclined bench in front of the pulldown machine, use a close-grip to do latfocused pulldowns.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hex Press
exercises.description:
• Engage the muscles
  • Position your feet wide
  • Controlled movement
  • Slow movement
  • Bring the weights toward your lower chest/stomach

exercises.name: Russian Push Ups
exercises.description:
Russian Push-Ups

Start in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lower your chest toward the floor, then shift your body forward while keeping your chest close to the ground. Extend your arms to return to the starting position, then reverse the movement smoothly. Keep your core tight and maintain controlled movement throughout the exercise.

exercises.name: Double Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: The double leg heel raise is important to strengthen and create control and stability around the ankle and knee, and provide balance and control for the hip and pelvis.

exercises.name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
exercises.description:
1. Start with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your torso. Keep your back straight with a slight bend in the knees and bend forward at the waist. Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor. Make sure to keep your head up. Your upper arms should be close to your torso and parallel to the floor. Your forearms should be pointed towards the floor as you hold the weights. There should be a 90-degree angle formed between your forearm and upper arm. This is your starting position.
  2. Now, while keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and use your triceps to lift the weights until the arm is fully extended. Focus on moving the forearm.
  3. After a brief pause at the top contraction, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
  4. Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

Variations: This exercise can be executed also one arm at a time much like the one arm rows are performed.

Also, if you like the one arm variety, you can use a low pulley handle instead of a dumbbell for better peak contraction. In this case, the palms should be facing up (supinated grip) as opposed to the torso (neutral grip).

exercises.name: Weighted Step-ups
exercises.description: box step ups w/ barbell and 45's on each side

exercises.name: Biceps with TRX
exercises.description: Grab the handles of the TRX straps, lean your body back, arms and legs extended, with your body positioned in a single straight line. (This is an arm exercise, not an abdominal one.)

exercises.name: YTWL Exercise
exercises.description:
• Purpose: Improves shoulder stability, posture, and scapular (shoulder blade) control. Often used in physical therapy and warm-ups.
  • Starting Position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips (like a deadlift) keeping your back flat, or lie face down on an incline bench. Keep your thumbs pointing up throughout.
  • Y (Arms up): Extend both arms straight forward and upward at a 135-degree angle from your body, forming a "Y". Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
  • T (Arms out): Open your arms straight out to the sides, perpendicular to your body, forming a "T". Focus on pinching your shoulder blades.
  • W (Arms bent): Pull your elbows back, bending them to 90 degrees, and squeeze your shoulder blades to form a "W". Keep your wrists firm.
  • L (Arms rotated): Start with elbows bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearms outward (external rotation) like a goalpost, forming an "L" or a gate.
  • Key Focus: Movements should be slow and controlled. Always lead with the thumbs and think about moving the shoulder blades, not just the arms.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown - Cross Body Single Arm
exercises.description: Sit at lat pulldown machine with body at a diagonal angle so that only one leg is under the pad. Pull the cable down with the opposite arm. this will force the cable to across your body while pulling down. Emphasises the stretch of the lat.

exercises.name: Sit & Reach
exercises.description: Sit on the ground with your legs extended straight in front of you. Reach both hands forward, trying to reach past your toes or as far as you can go. Return to the starting position and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Rotations
exercises.description:
Dumbbell shoulder rotations are designed to strengthen the rotator cuff muscles and improve shoulder stability and mobility.

  1. External Rotation: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, keeping your elbow stationary. Slowly return to the starting position.
  2. Internal Rotation: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm inward, toward your body, and slowly return to the starting position. Perform the exercise with controlled movements to avoid strain.

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Press
exercises.description: A single arm exercise that starts with the hand close to the chest with with the elbows bent, and the elbow flared out. Press forward and down against the cable straightening the elbow.

exercises.name: Sit Up Elbow Thrust
exercises.description: This is a top down rotation movement, and it’s a bit more explosive, too. Lying with knees bent and feet on the floor, sit up and then drive your left elbow across your entire body toward the right, then come back to center and then finally lower yourself down. Then hit the other side.

exercises.name: Cable Fly Middle Chest
exercises.description:
Execution

  1. Start position: Arms extended out to your sides (a big “T” shape), feeling a stretch in your chest.

  2. Movement: Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide hugging motion.

    • Focus on squeezing your chest at the center.
    • Do not lock your elbows or turn it into a press.

  3. Return: Slowly open your arms back to the start, maintaining tension on the chest.

exercises.name: Squat Jumps
exercises.description: Jump wide, then close

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.description: On all fours. Arch spine up (cat) then drop it down (cow). Breathe with movement.

exercises.name: Chest Press
exercises.description:
1. Adjust the seat height so that the grips are parallel to your chest.
  2. Use your legs to push the foot forward pedal.
  3. Bring the handles to the start position.
  4. Keep your back in contact with the back pad, press outwards.
  5. Press the handles away from your chest and exhale.
  6. Allow the handles to come in gently until they reach your chest.
  7. Allow the handles to return to your chest as you inhale.

exercises.name: TRX/Rings Face Pull
exercises.description:
1. Set TRX straps or rings at about head to mid-chest height. Stand facing the anchor and hold one handle or ring in each hand with a neutral grip.
  2. Walk the feet toward the anchor and lean back until the arms are extended in front of you and the body forms a straight line from head to heels.
  3. Brace the core and glutes. Soften the knees slightly and keep the ribs down.
  4. Pull the handles or rings toward the face by driving the elbows high and wide, roughly to ear height. Externally rotate the shoulders so the hands finish near the temples or just outside the ears, thumbs pointing back if the straps allow.
  5. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of the pull without shrugging toward the ears. Pause briefly.
  6. Extend the arms under control back to the start and repeat.

Keep constant tension in the straps. A steeper lean increases difficulty; a more upright stance makes it easier.

exercises.name: kettlebell sumo deadlift
exercises.description: Place your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, pointing your toes outward. Keep your back straight, shoulders back, and chest up. The knees must follow the same direction as the toes and not move forward. When going up, it is advisable to contract your glutes to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise..

exercises.name: Barbell Full Squat
exercises.description:
• The barbell full squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups in the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.
  • Proper form is crucial for maximizing results and preventing injuries during the barbell full squat. This includes maintaining a shoulder-width stance, creating whole body tension, controlling your descent, and maintaining proper depth and knee positioning.
  • Assistance moves such as the front squat, goblet squat, split squat, and Bulgarian split squat can help improve your performance in the barbell full squat by targeting specific muscle groups and improving overall technique.
  • To achieve new personal records in your back squat, gradually increase weight over time, vary rep ranges and sets to stimulate muscle growth, and prioritize rest and recovery between training sessions.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description:
The reverse cable fly, also known as the cable rear delt fly, is a deltoid muscle strengthening and definition exercise. It’s one of the best isolation exercises for your back and posterior deltoid.This workout targets your posterior (back) deltoids while using a range of upper body muscles.

  1. Adjust the weight and the pulleys to the right height. You should be able to see the pulleys because they should be above your head.
  2. With your right hand, grab the left pulley, and with your left hand, grab the right pulley, crossing them in front of you. This is where you’ll begin your journey.
  3. Start the movement by moving your arms back and forth while keeping your arms straight.
  4. Pause at the finish of the move for a brief moment before returning the handles to their starting positions.

exercises.name: Upright Row, SZ-bar
exercises.description: Stand straight, your feet are shoulder-width apart. Hold the SZ-bar with an overhand grip on your thighs, the arms are stretched. Lift the bar close to the body till your chin. The elbows point out so that at the highest point they form a V. Make here a short pause before going slowly down and repeating the movement.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant Circles
exercises.description:
Fire Hydrant Circles
Part of: Limber 11
Source: Joe DeFranco
Prescription: 10 forward / 10 backward
Type: dynamic

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Sit at a plate-loaded (lever) lat pulldown machine with your thighs secured under the pads. Grip the handles overhead with arms fully extended. Pull the handles down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back, squeezing your lats at the bottom. Return slowly to full extension. Resistance comes from weight plates loaded on the machine's lever arms rather than a cable stack.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
exercises.description:
1. Lay down
  2. Place your hands near your butt (often slightly in front or under or both)
  3. Raise your legs, but about 70% of the way you should be able to also raise your pelvis
  4. (optional/variable) Hold 1/2 seconds at the top
  5. Go back to starting position

exercises.name: Stationary bike cardio
exercises.description:
Benefits of Stationary Bike Cardio

Stationary bike cardio is an excellent form of exercise that offers multiple benefits for health and well-being. Here are some of the most notable ones:

Improved Cardiovascular Health

  • Strengthens the heart: Regular exercise helps improve the heart's efficiency and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.
  • Increases circulation: It improves blood flow, which can help lower blood pressure.

Calorie Burning and Weight Loss

  • Efficient for burning calories: Depending on the intensity, you can burn between 400 and 600 calories per hour.
  • Helps with weight loss: Combined with a balanced diet, stationary bike cardio can be effective for losing weight.

Muscle Strengthening

  • Tones the legs: It mainly works the leg muscles, including the quadriceps, hamstrings and calves.
  • Improves muscular endurance: Over time, you can increase the endurance and strength in your legs.

Mental Health Benefits

  • Reduces stress: Exercise releases endorphins, which can improve your mood and reduce stress.
  • Boosts energy: Regular physical activity can raise your energy levels and improve sleep quality.

exercises.name: Side plank right
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Lie down on your side, with your bottom elbow at a right angle, arm sticking out. Lift your pelvis off the floor by lifting your bottom shoulder up, keeping the forearm on the floor; your head, pelvis, and feet should be in a straight line.

Steps:

  1. Hold this position.

exercises.name: Pull-up Isometric Hold
exercises.description: Hold the pull-up movement in any position

exercises.name: One Arm Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
exercises.description:
Set the pulley at the bottom of the cable machine and grab onto it without using any attachments. Extend the cable directly overhead.

While keeping your back straight and upper arm stationary, lower the cable behind your head until you feel a good stretch in your triceps, and then extend it back upward until your elbow is locked out.

exercises.name: Leg Presses (narrow)
exercises.description:
The exercise is very similar to the wide leg press:

Sit on the machine and put your feet on the platform so far apart  that you could just put another foot in between them. The feet are parallel and point up.

Lower the weight so much, that the knees form a right angle. Push immediately the platform up again, without any pause. When in the lower position, the knees point a bit outwards and the movement should be always fluid.

exercises.name: Leg Raises, Standing
exercises.description: Put your forearms on the pads on the leg raise machine, the body is hanging freely. Lift now your legs with a fast movement as high as you can, make a short pause of 1sec at the top, and bring them down again. Make sure that during the exercise your body does not swing, only the legs should move.

exercises.name: Chin-up Isometric Hold
exercises.description:
Grip the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) and pull yourself up until your chin is at or above the bar.

Hold this top position for the set time, keeping your core tight, your shoulders stable and your body still.

exercises.name: Reverse Snow Angel
exercises.description: Lay flat on your stomach with your arms extended in front of you on the ground as your legs are lying flat. Lift both your arms and move them to your side slowly. Then, move them back.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Squat with Dumbbells
exercises.description: The Bulgarian split squat consists of performing a squat on one leg with the rear foot resting on a raised platform. Elevating your back leg on a bench creates instability and increases the range of motion of the exercise.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position

Step into the captain's chair (vertical knee raise station). Rest your forearms on the pads and hold the handles. Keep your upper body upright, look straight ahead and press your back against the pad, without rounding or arching it. Your legs are almost straight with a slight bend in the knees, your feet are off the floor and your legs are together.

Movement

Pull your bent legs up, bringing your knees towards your chest. Only go as high as you can while keeping good form, with your legs together the whole time. Then lower your legs again while inhaling, without putting your feet back on the floor.

exercises.name: Reverse lunges
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Stand straight, feet hip-width apart.

Steps:

  1. Step backward with one leg so it can bend comfortably to a 90 degree angle.
  2. Slowly bend both knees to form 90 degree angles.
  3. Return to the starting position.
  4. Repeat, alternating legs.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.description: The leg extension is a resistance weight training exercise that targets the quadriceps muscle in the legs. The exercise is done using a machine called the Leg Extension Machine. There are various manufacturers of these machines and each one is slightly different. Most gym and weight rooms will have the machine in their facility. The leg extension is an isolated exercise targeting one specific muscle group, the quadriceps. It should not be considered as a total leg workout, such as the squat or deadlift. The exercise consists of bending the leg at the knee and extending the legs, then lowering them back to the original position.

exercises.name: Trap-3 Raise
exercises.description:
1. Hinge forwards and bend your knees slightly. Depress and retract the shoulder you will use. Rest the other hand on your knee.
  2. Raise your hand about 15 degrees overhead, maintaining the position of your shoulder.

exercises.name: Lateral Raises
exercises.description: This exercise works the deltoid muscle of the shoulder. The movement starts with the arms straight, and the hands holding weights at the sides or in front of the body. Body is in a slight forward-leaning position with hips and knees bent a little. Arms are kept straight or slightly bent, and raised through an arc of movement in the coronal plane that terminates when the hands are at approximately shoulder height. Weights are lowered to the starting position, completing one rep. When using a cable machine the individual stands with the coronal plane in line with the pulley, which is at or near the ground.[9] The exercise can be completed one shoulder at a time (with the other hand used to stabilize the body against the weight moved), or with both hands simultaneously if two parallel pulleys are available.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description:
The Bird Dog is a core stability exercise that enhances balance, coordination, and spinal alignment. It’s a low-impact movement ideal for strengthening the posterior chain and improving overall functional control.

  1. Begin on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, keeping your spine neutral.
  2. Extend your right arm forward and left leg backward simultaneously, keeping hips square.
  3. Pause briefly at full extension while engaging your core and glutes.
  4. Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side

exercises.name: Hamstring Chokes
exercises.description: Sit on the ground and bend one leg, bringing your knee toward you. Place your hand behind your hamstring and gently pull your leg toward your chest, feeling a stretch in the back of your thigh. Straighten your leg, extending up toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Close-grip Lat Pull Down
exercises.description: Grip the pull-down bar with your hands closer than shoulder width apart, with your palms facing away from you. Lean back slightly. Pull the bar down towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides as you come down. Pull your shoulders back at the end of the motion.

exercises.name: Pause Bench
exercises.description: Lower the bar to your chest and pause (but do not rest) there for 2 seconds. Press back up. use the same weight you would on bench press, but perform only single reps. Total the number of reps you did in one set of bench press (if you did 3 sets of 8 do 8 sinlge pause bench reps.

exercises.name: Barbell Silverback Shrug
exercises.description:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart holding the barbell with both hands in front just past shoulder width.
  2. Bend forward at the hips with a slight bend in your knees, keeping your back straight.
  3. Engage your shoulder blades, as if you are trying to touch them together.
  4. Release the shrug. Description taken from MuscleWiki

exercises.name: Black Widow Knee Slides
exercises.description: In this bottom-up rotation exercise movement, you’ll cross your knee over and drive it into that opposite elbow. Start in high plank position (or tabletop position) with hands directly beneath your shoulders. Lift the left knee toward the right arm and slide it up the forearm to get more of that posterior pelvic tilt and engagement of the abdominal muscles. Then do the opposite side, bringing your right knee toward your left hand.

exercises.name: Run - Treadmill
exercises.description: Run on a treadmill

exercises.name: Pogo jumps
exercises.description: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. Perform quick, low vertical jumps using primarily your ankles. Keep your torso upright, minimise knee bending and aim for short ground contact times. Land on the balls of your feet and immediately rebound into the next jump.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and bending forward at the hips while keeping the back straight, then returning to a standing position. It primarily targets the hamstrings and glutes.

exercises.name: Leg Presses (wide)
exercises.description:
Sit on the machine and put your feet on the platform, a bit more than shoulder wide. The feet are turned outwards by a few degrees.

Lower the weight so much, that the knees form a right angle. Push immediately the platform up again, without any pause. When in the lower position, the knees point a bit outwards and the movement should be always fluid.

exercises.name: Ice cream maker
exercises.description: From the final phase of a pull-up, we push ourselves back with our shoulders until we reach the front lever position. From there, we pull ourselves back up to the starting position.

exercises.name: Shoulder dislocates
exercises.description:
Starting position: Stand up with your back straight and a resistance band, towel, or broomstick handle in hand. With your hands straight in front of your body and the band between your hands, push your hands apart to both be at around 45 degrees from your body, thumbs facing down. If using a towel or broomstick handle instead, grab it with an overhand grip. Steps:

  1. Keeping your arms outstretched, rotate at the shoulders to bring your arms overhead and then down toward your glutes.
  2. Rotate at the shoulders in the opposite direction — overhead and then toward your groin.
  3. Repeat.

exercises.name: TRX Obliques
exercises.description:
1. Place your feet in the stirrups and assume a high plank with your hands directly beneath your shoulders.
  2. Pull your knees to your right elbow, then push them back out and to the centre.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: The leg press is a weight training exercise in which the individual pushes a weight or resistance away from them using their legs.

exercises.name: Hamstring Kicks
exercises.description: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and extend one arm in front of you. Swing that leg up in front of you and back down while keeping your leg as straight as possible and your toes pointed up.Repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: Medicine ball twist
exercises.description: In a seated position, the torso is rotated from side to side without forcing, approaching the knees and making the ball touch the ground from time to time

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description: Lay flat on your stomach with your arms extended in front of you on the ground as your legs are lying flat. Lift both your arms and legs at the same time, as if you were flying, and contract the lower back. Make sure that you are breathing and, depending on your fitness level, hold the movement for at least two to five seconds per repetition.

exercises.name: Glute Kickback (Machine)
exercises.description:
Drive through your heel, not your toes, to hit the glute.

Don’t hyperextend your lower back at the top.

exercises.name: Recovery Bobbing
exercises.description: Same motion as the Bobbing Exhale Drill, but done in slightly deeper water (so you're not touching the bottom) and at a slower, more relaxed pace — think of it as a recovery/reset exercise rather than a hard drill. Use it between harder drills to reset your breathing rhythm and calm down if you're feeling rushed or out of sync.

exercises.name: Standing biceps stretch right
exercises.description: Stand with your right arm close to a wall. Extend your right arm and put your right hand on the wall, then gently turn your body to the left.

exercises.name: Finger Pushup
exercises.description:
1. Hand Positioning:
  • Start in a plank position with your hands directly beneath your shoulders.
  • Spread your fingers wide apart, placing them firmly on the ground.
  1. Finger Placement:
  • Gradually lift your palms off the ground, shifting the weight onto your fingers.
  • Focus on distributing the load evenly across your fingertips and thumbs.
  1. Body Alignment:
  • Maintain a straight line from head to heels to engage your core.
  • Keep your body in a controlled and stable position throughout the exercise.
  1. Lowering Phase:
  • Slowly bend your elbows, lowering your chest towards the ground.
  • Ensure controlled movement, maintaining stability on your fingertips.
  1. Pushing Up:
  • Press through your fingertips to straighten your arms, returning to the starting position.
  • Emphasize the engagement of your fingers and thumbs throughout the push-up.

exercises.name: Landmine Squat to Press
exercises.description:
• Bar Position: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a secure corner.

  • Stance: Stand facing the barbell with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width. Turn your toes out 10–35 degrees to allow for better pelvic movement and depth.

  • Grip: Cup the free end of the barbell with both hands (fingers interlaced or overlapping) and hold it at mid-chest level, just below the collarbone.

  • Descent: Brace your core and sit back into a squat, keeping your chest up and weight on your heels.

  • Depth: Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor. A good reference is when your elbows touch the tops of your thighs or just inside your knees.

  • Posture: Ensure your back remains flat and your spine neutral throughout the movement.

  • Drive: Powerfully drive through your heels to stand up. Use the momentum from your legs to "thrust" the weight upward.

  • Extension: In one fluid motion, press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended. At the top, your biceps should be near your ears.

  • The "Lean": As you reach the top of the press, lean slightly forward into the bar to encourage proper upward rotation of the shoulder blades and avoid lower back arching.

Slowly lower the barbell back to chest height in a controlled manner before immediately beginning the next repetition.

exercises.name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Sitting on a bench, grab a barbell with your palms facing down and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees.

Curl your knuckles towards your face, lifting the barbell. Pause for a moment in the top position, then slowly return the barbell to the starting position.

exercises.name: JM Press
exercises.description: The JM press keeps your shoulders stationary, relying on the elbow flexion and extension to move the weight using your triceps strength. That means you get all the benefits of the best triceps-strengthening exercises without overtaxing that delicate shoulder joint. Classic win-win!

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
exercises.description:
Lie face-down on a bench with your legs hanging off the edge.

  1. Bend your hips so your thighs are vertical, bending your knees at the same time so your shins stay horizontal.
  2. Straighten out your legs so they are not bent and your toes are pointing backwards horizontally.
  3. Return to the original position, and repeat.

exercises.name: Front Raises with Plates
exercises.description:
The plate front raise is a variation of the dumbbell front raise where the lifter holds a weight plate between two hands, rather than using a dumbbell, barbell, or other weight. It can provide variety in a shoulder-focused muscle-building workout, or as part of an upper body or full-body circuit.

  1. While standing straight, hold a barbell plate in both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Your palms should be facing each other and your arms should be extended and locked with a slight bend at the elbows and the plate should be down near your waist in front of you as far as you can go. Tip: The arms will remain in this position throughout the exercise. This will be your starting position.
  2. Slowly raise the plate as you exhale until it is a little above shoulder level. Hold the contraction for a second. As you inhale, slowly lower the plate back down to the starting position.
  3. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Push-Up
exercises.description: Normal Push-ups on Dumbbells, this brings a further range of movement

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A glute bridge, where you use just one leg at a time.

exercises.name: Long Lunge Pulse Stretch
exercises.description:
1. Hold the resistance band (or any other rope-like object, the elasticity is not necessary) above your head, between your hands, with your arms straight. Pull it taught to engage your lats.
  2. Step forwards into a lunge, dropping until your knee is almost touching the floor.
  3. Slowly and controlledly pulse your body up and down by about an inch. Repeat for required reps.
  4. Repeat for other leg.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.description: The seated dumbbell calf raise is a targeted exercise for strengthening the lower leg muscles. It follows the same movement pattern as the machine version: you place the weight on your knees, and by extending and flexing your ankles, you move the weight.

exercises.name: Backward arm circles
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Stand tall with your back straight.

Steps:

  1. Keeping your arms straight, bring them in front of you, raise them over your head, then continue the motion behind your back and down to the initial position.
  2. Keep circling your arms as described in step 1.

exercises.name: Delt Stretch
exercises.description: Stretch your deltoids for a certain period of time.

exercises.name: Hip Bridge
exercises.description:
Get into bridge position, balance yourself on heels and start extending legs unilaterally.

Keep hip extended as much as possible.

exercises.name: Floor Skull Crusher
exercises.description: Allowing you to safely load more weight than a regular skull crusher, lie on the floor and rest the weight on the floor in between each repetition.

exercises.name: Seated Band Row
exercises.description: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you and your back tall. Loop a resistance band around the soles of both feet and hold one end in each hand, arms extended and a slight bend in the knees. Pull the band toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows straight back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your chest up and your torso still rather than rocking backward to move the band. Extend the arms slowly to return. Because the torso stays upright and supported, this is a useful row when a bent-over position is uncomfortable, and it needs no anchor point.

exercises.name: One Arm Bent Row
exercises.description: One arm bent over row on cable with a machine

exercises.name: Reach ups
exercises.description: To perform this exercise, lie on your back with your arms extended overhead. Then, contract your abdominals and lift your torso off the floor while reaching your arms toward the ceiling to "reach" as high as possible. Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the movement. Reach ups strengthen the abdominal muscles and improve the flexibility of the spine. They can be incorporated into a variety of training routines to work on core strength and stability.

exercises.name: Alternate Walking
exercises.description: 1m30s of walking (~4.5 km/h) to 30 s of jog (7 km/h) and repeat

exercises.name: Triceps on Machine
exercises.description: Sit down and hold the bar firmly with your hands. Now press the weight upwards (don't fully extend your arms) and lower it slowly again. As with other triceps exercises, it's important not to move your upper arms.

exercises.name: Swimming 50m sprints
exercises.description: 50m swimming sprints at 1min

exercises.name: Ring Support Hold
exercises.description: Hold yourself in a support position on gymnastic rings with arms straight at sides. Focus on keeping rings turned out slightly and maintaining hollow body position. This is an isometric hold for chest, shoulders, and triceps.

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic Curl
exercises.description: Natural Leg Extension is alternative to Leg Extension machine with no equipment.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand)
exercises.description:
Execution

  1. Starting position:

    • Hold the barbell with arms fully extended toward the floor.
    • Maintain tension in your lats and back muscles.

exercises.name: Run - Interval Training
exercises.description: Run and do some interval trainings such as hill repat, fartlek,..

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Side Lateral
exercises.description: seated slightly leaned forward at beginning of exercise

exercises.name: Incline DB Y-Raise (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Incline DB Y-Raise with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Side Lateral (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Seated Dumbbell Side Lateral with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Kneeling kickbacks
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Get down on all fours.

Steps:

  1. Push one foot back until fully extended, concentrating on the gluteus muscles.
  2. Stay for one second, then return to the initial position.
  3. Repeat, alternating feet.

exercises.name: Cross-Bench Dumbbell Pullovers
exercises.description: Grasp a moderately weighted dumbbell so your palms are flat against the underside of the top plates and your thumbs are around the bar. Lie on your back across a flat bench so only your upper back and shoulders are in contact with the bench. Your feet should be set about shoulder-width apart and your head should hang slightly downward. With the dumbbell supported at arm's length directly about your chest, bend your arms about 15 degrees and keep them bent throughout the movement. Slowly lower the dumbbell backward and downward in a semicircle arc to as low a position as is comfortably possible. Raise it slowly back along the same arc to the starting point, and repeat for the required number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise with a small bar
exercises.description:
The Cable Front Raise with a small bar isolates your anterior deltoids (front shoulders) by providing constant tension, requiring you to stand facing away from a low pulley, grab the bar with an overhand grip, and lift it in front of you to shoulder height with slightly bent arms, avoiding swinging and keeping your core tight for controlled movement up and down. Use a light-to-moderate weight, focusing on slow, controlled reps to feel the muscle work, not momentum.

How to Perform the Cable Front Raise (Bar)

Setup: Attach a small straight bar to a low cable pulley. Set the weight to a light or moderate setting.

Starting Position: Stand with your back to the machine, holding the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at hip level, arms extended but not locked. Feet shoulder-width apart, core braced, shoulders back and down.

The Lift: Exhale and slowly raise the bar straight up in front of you, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until your hands reach shoulder height (or slightly below).

The Hold: Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your front delts.

The Lower: Inhale as you slowly and controllably lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining tension.

exercises.name: Child's pose
exercises.description:
Starting position:

Start on all fours, knees, toes, and hands touching the ground. Your two big toes should be touching.

Steps:

  1. Move your knees so that they're about hip-width apart.
  2. On an exhale, move your pelvis back to sit on your heels. Your hands should still be touching the ground.
  3. Relax your upper body, lowering your forehead to the floor and letting your hands move forward naturally.
  4. Stay in this pose.

Tips:

  • To leave the pose, walk your arms back under your shoulders and move your upper body up into a seated position.

exercises.name: Sitting Calf Raises
exercises.description: Sit on a bench for calf raises and check that the feet are half free and that you can completely stretch the calf muscles down. Pull your calves up, going as far (up) as you can. Make at the highest point a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds and go down.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: Triceps pushdown on cable using lat bar.

exercises.name: Side-Kick Breathing (Kickboard)
exercises.description: Push off the wall on your side (not flat on your stomach), one arm extended forward holding the board or just extended, kicking continuously. Keep your head in a neutral position looking at the bottom of the pool, and when you need air, rotate your head sideways (one ear stays in the water, other faces up) to breathe, then rotate back to neutral. Swim a length like this, then repeat on the other side. This teaches the exact head position and rotation you'll use once full stroke breathing comes in.

exercises.name: Reverse Wood Chops
exercises.description:
• Attach a looping resistance band to a rack below knee height
  • Grip the other end of the band like holding a baseball bat with both hands
  • Stretch the band facing it
  • Start with your hands at the side of your hips, knees bent
  • Rotate your hips while moving your hands towards over the top of your opposite shoulder
  • Imagine the motion as striking a baseball with a bat

exercises.name: Rice Bucket Training
exercises.description: Fill a deep bucket with dry rice. Push your hand into the rice and repeatedly open and close your fist, twist your wrist both ways, and spread your fingers against the rice for the set time. This is a low impact way to train every muscle of the hand and forearm and is good for warming up or recovery.

exercises.name: Bent-over Lateral Raises
exercises.description: Sit on bench while holding weights. Bend forward as far as possible, with arms slightly bent at the elbow. Perform a lateral raise while maintaining the bend in your elbow.

exercises.name: Dips (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Dips with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Box Handstand Push-up
exercises.description: Pike push-up with legs on an elevated surface. Progression to handstand push-up.

exercises.name: Upper External Oblique
exercises.description: Exercise for upper external oblique muscles

exercises.name: Cable Press Around
exercises.description:
Set the cable pulley at chest height and attach a D-handle bar. Grab the handle with a neutral grip and hold it next to your chest with your elbow fully flexed and tight to your side. Turn away from the pulley so your torso is at 45 degrees.

Hold the other side of the functional trainer with your corresponding hand. Assume a staggered stance for better balance.

While keeping your chest proud, extend your elbow at 45 degrees across your midline while keeping your arm parallel to the floor. Stop shy of lockout and contract your chest at the top of the range of motion (ROM).

exercises.name: Exercise Band Plantarflexion
exercises.description: Banded plantarflexion is a great way to bridge the gap between plantarflexion range of motion and the more strenuous calf raises in weight bearing. This can help strengthen the calf muscles, load the Achilles tendon, and improve plantarflexion range of motion.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Reverse Fly
exercises.description: The incline dumbbell reverse fly is an upper-body exercise targeting the posterior or rear deltoids, as well as the postural muscles of the upper back. Because it targets such small muscles, this exercise is usually performed with light weight for high reps, such as 10-15 reps per set or more.

exercises.name: Shoulder width three-point push-up
exercises.description: Get into a push-up position with your shoulders directly above your hands and your feet hip-width apart. Draw your belly button in towards your spine and tighten your abdominal muscles. Lift your left foot about five centimetres off the floor. Point your toes straight down. Do not move your hips. Your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the exercise. Now bend your elbows, lower your chest to the floor and push yourself back up. Repeat the exercise on the other side.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.description: Pectoral issolation exercise - full range of motion is best with full contraction and slow negative

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.description:
Execution

  1. Hinge at the hips:

    • Push your hips backward, keeping a slight bend in the knees (soft knees).
    • Lower the barbell along the front of your thighs/shins while maintaining a neutral spine.
    • Keep the bar close to your body.

exercises.name: Side Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
• Begin by lying down on your side with your top leg straight and your bottom leg bent for support.
  • Lift your top leg off the ground
  • (optional) - Hold position at the top

Resources:

  • 40 seconds YouTube video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g9FtnmsIYgI

exercises.name: Shrugs, Dumbbells
exercises.description:
Stand with straight body, the hands are hanging freely on the side and hold each a dumbbell. Lift from this position the shoulders as high as you can, but don't bend the arms during the movement. On the highest point, make a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds before returning slowly to the initial position.

When training with a higher weight, make sure that you still do the whole movement!

exercises.name: seated figure four
exercises.description: Seat on  a bench. Feet flat on the ground. Place your left ankle over your right knee. Your right knee stays flat. Keep your back straight. Gently push your left knee down.

exercises.name: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press
exercises.description: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press, chest press movement focusing on the triceps. DB stays parallel with body

exercises.name: DB Wrist Extension
exercises.description:
Grab two dumbbells with an overhand grip and lay your forearms across your knees.

Let your wrists flex fully, then extend your wrists.

exercises.name: Upright Row, on Multi Press
exercises.description:
The movements are basically the same as with an SZ-bar, but you use the bar on the multi press:

Stand straight, your feet are shoulder-width apart. Hold the bar with an overhand grip on your thighs, the arms are stretched. Lift the bar close to the body till your chin. The elbows point out so that at the highest point they form a V. Make here a short pause before going slowly down and repeating the movement.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.description: Start with landmine barbell straight up by using your shoulders to push it up above you. Then, from that position, bring it your side to target your abdominals and return to starting position.

exercises.name: Dynamic Planche
exercises.description:
1. Start in a plank position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet hip-width apart.
  2. Engage your core to keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
  3. From this position, bend your knees slightly and jump with both feet inward, bringing them as close to your core as possible
  4. As soon as your feet touch the ground, push off forcefully to jump again and return to the starting plank position.
  5. Continue repeating this jumping motion, maintaining control and core stability throughout the exercise.
  6. Make sure to keep your breathing steady while jumping, breathing deeply and controlling your breathing.
  7. Keep your gaze fixed on the ground to maintain proper spinal alignment.
  8. Repeat the jumps for the desired length of time or the number of repetitions recommended for your workout program.
  9. To finish the exercise, rest by releasing the plank position, then stretch if necessary to loosen your muscles.

exercises.name: Incline Shoulder Press Up
exercises.description:
1. Place your hands on the bench in a press up position
  2. Push your chest away from the bench to separate your shoulder blades
