exercises.name: Rowing Machine
exercises.description: Sit on a rowing machine with your back straight.

exercises.name: Butterfly (Custom)
exercises.description: Perform Butterfly with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

exercises.name: Clamshell to Reverse Clamshell
exercises.description:
Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your legs stacked. Lift your top knee into a clamshell position and keep the leg elevated throughout the movement. From there, alternate between opening the knee upward and lifting the foot upward, moving through hip external and internal rotation.

Keep the movement slow and controlled. Do not let the top leg rest on the bottom leg between repetitions.

exercises.name: High Row
exercises.description: Kneeling down on one leg and pulling cable down while driving elbow into the lats.

exercises.name: Incline OHP DB
exercises.description:
• Sit on a bench with 45° incline
  • Ellbows 45° out
  • Move dumbbells down until upper arms are parallel to shoulders
  • Move dumbbells up, meeting overhead

exercises.name: One Arm Triceps Extensions on Cable
Cable Cupping
exercises.description: Attach a single handle to a low cable. Rest your forearm on a bench or your thigh with the palm facing up and the cable pulling your hand away from you. Curl your fingers and wrist toward you as if cupping a ball, squeeze for a second, then lower slowly. This builds the wrist flexion used to control an opponent's hand in arm wrestling.

exercises.name: TRX gorilla biceps curl
exercises.description: We'll stand facing the TRX straps and grab them with our fists facing each other, facing forward, with our arms fully extended at about shoulder-width apart. We'll keep our body straight, backward, as in the previous exercises, since we'll be lifting our body toward the TRX straps by activating our biceps. Our body will be straight, with our feet flat on the floor. This time, we'll place our arms open to the sides and at chest height. The movement we'll perform is a contraction toward our chest. To achieve this, we'll bend our elbows so that, by activating our biceps, we can pull our body toward the straps.

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrug
exercises.description: The shoulder shrug (usually called simply the shrug) is an exercise in weight training used to develop the upper trapezius muscle. The lifter stands erect, hands about shoulder width apart, and raises the shoulders as high as possible, and then lowers them, while not bending the elbows, or moving the body at all. The lifter may not have as large a range of motion as in a normal shrug done for active flexibility. It is usually considered good form if the slope of the shoulders is horizontal in the elevated position.

exercises.name: Prisoner Squat
exercises.description: Stand upright with your chest slightly raised, your feet hip-width apart and your toes pointing straight ahead. Bring your hands to the back of your head with your fingers slightly interlaced and your elbows pointing to the side. Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your upper body as upright as possible.  Push your knees outwards, they must never point towards each other. If your upper body moves slightly forward, make sure that it does not bend. Always keep your elbows level with your ears by tensing the muscles between your shoulder blades. If you are flexible enough, you can sink down until your buttocks touch your calves. However, make sure that you do not bend your spine.  Before this happens, reverse the movement and use your heels and glutes to push yourself upwards with so much momentum that your feet lift off briefly and you do a little hop.  If necessary, correct the position of your feet, arms and upper body before you move on to the next repetition. exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance with Eyes Closed
exercises.description: A balance and proprioception drill. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and the other foot lifted clear of the floor, then close your eyes and hold the position. Without visual feedback the ankle and hip stabilisers have to do the work, so expect noticeable wobble. Stand within reach of a wall, counter or chair so you can steady yourself if needed. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. Commonly prescribed in rehabilitation after ankle or knee injury.

exercises.name: Bodyweight lunge HD
exercises.description: Bodyweight lunges are an effective calisthenic exercise for strengthening the lower body, improving balance and stability, and developing functional strength. They are a popular choice for bodyweight workouts, home workouts, and can also be included as part of a larger strength training routine.

exercises.name: Supported Deep Squat Hold
exercises.description: Hold a stable support in front of you and lower into a comfortable deep squat with both feet grounded. Use the support for balance and to control depth. Maintain the squat hold without bouncing or forcing the hips or ankles farther than a comfortable range.

exercises.name: ankle dorsiflexion rocks
exercises.description: Move your knee forward, keeping your heel on the ground. Hold the position for a couple of seconds and return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Side split squats right
exercises.description:
Starting position:

  1. Stand tall and take a wide lateral stride, just greater than shoulder width.

Steps:

  1. Bend one knee until your thigh is parallel to the floor. The bent knee must be in line with the foot.
  2. Push back to the starting position.
  3. Repeat.

exercises.name: Marching High Knees
exercises.description:
A low-impact cardio and mobility exercise that strengthens the hip flexors and improves balance.

  1. ​Movement: Stand tall and lift one knee toward your chest as high as comfortable.
  2. ​Arms: Swing the opposite arm forward as you lift your knee, similar to a walking motion.
  3. ​Core: Keep your abs engaged to maintain an upright posture.
  4. ​Pace: Perform the movement with control, alternating legs rhythmically.

exercises.name: Deep breathing (standing or seated)
exercises.description: A conscious breathing technique to improve oxygenation, reduce stress and connect with the present moment.

exercises.name: Hamstring Foam roller
exercises.description: Move your hamstrings slowly over the foam roller

exercises.name: Bench Dips On Floor HD
exercises.description: Triceps dips on floor are a compound exercise as they worked multiple muscle groups simultaneously. Although this bodyweight exercise mainly targets the triceps, it also hits your chest and front of your shoulder. Triceps dips on floor are one of the most effective exercises to increase arm strength and also build lean muscle in your upper arms. Triceps dips on floor are a closed kinetic chain exercise and express that you do the movements around a fixed point. It increases compression force on your joints thereby improving stability.

exercises.name: Tricep Rope Pushdowns
exercises.description:
• Setup: Stand facing the cable, feet shoulder-width apart, with a slight forward lean.
  • Grip: Hold the rope with palms facing each other and elbows tucked tight to your ribs.
  • Execution: Push the rope down until arms are fully straight, pulling the ends apart at the bottom.
  • Control: Keep upper arms still and return to the start with a slow, controlled motion.

exercises.name: Incline Close Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Narrower grip than regular bench press, just outside shoulder width.

exercises.name: Banded Ankle Mobility
exercises.description:
Anchor a resistance band low behind you, for example at the bottom of a rack, and loop it around the front of your ankle, just above the foot.

Get into a half-kneeling position with the banded foot in front, so that the band pulls your ankle backwards.

Keeping your heel on the floor, drive your knee forward over your toes, then return under control. Repeat for several reps and switch sides.

exercises.name: bicycle crunches
exercises.description: Bicycle crunches are a core exercise performed on the floor. Lie on your back with your hands behind your head and legs extended. Lift your shoulders off the ground, bring one knee toward your chest, and twist your torso so your opposite elbow meets the knee. Alternate sides in a pedaling motion, ensuring controlled movements and engaging your core throughout the exercise.

exercises.name: Dumbbell wide bicep curls
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and palms facing forward. Bend your elbows and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders. Slowly return and repeat.

exercises.name: Leverage Machine Iso Row
exercises.description: Adjust seat height so that the handles are at the bottom of your pectorals or just below.

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description:
-Laying on the back, lift your straightened legs from the ground at a 45 degree angle.

-As your Left foot travels downward and nearly touches the floor, your Right foot should seek to reach a 90 degree angle, or as close to one as possible.

-Bring your R foot down until it nearly touches the floor, and bring your L foot upwards.  Maintain leg rigidity throughout the exercise.  Your head should stay off the ground, supported by tightened upper abdominals.

-(L up R down, L down R up, x2)  ^v, v^, ^v, v^ = 1 rep

-Primarily works the Rectus Abdominus, the hip flexors and the lower back. Secondarily works the Obliques.  Emphasis placed on the lower quadrant of the abs.

exercises.name: Clap Push-UP
exercises.description:
The clap push-up is an explosive upper body movement that builds power and fast-twitch muscle strength. It adds a plyometric challenge to the traditional push-up by requiring the hands to leave the ground mid-rep.

  1. Start in a strong push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and core engaged
  2. Lower your body explosively and push off the ground with enough force to lift your hands.
  3. Quickly clap your hands together at chest level before returning them to the floor.
  4. Land with soft elbows to absorb the impact and immediately move into the next rep

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.description:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointed forward, and chest tall.
  2. Extend your leg straight out; extend both arms in front of you, at shoulder level. Brace your core and look straight ahead.
  3. Slowly squat down.
  4. (optional) pause at the bottom.

Keep your (free) leg and arms extended for the whole duration.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Clean and Press
exercises.description: Full-body muscles building exercise. This exercise provides a huge range of benefits in terms of strength & size and is extremely functional.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Ulnar Deviation
exercises.description: Stand with your arm straight down by your side. Hold a dumbbell by one end of the handle with the weighted end pointing behind you. Keeping the arm still, lift the weighted end up behind you using only the wrist, then lower it slowly. This is the opposite of wrist rising and keeps the wrist balanced.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lunge with Kettlebell:
exercises.description:
How to do a single-leg kettlebell lunge

Preparation: Stand with your feet together. Hold the kettlebell with both hands by the handle, keeping it close to your chest, or hold it with one hand (on the same side as the working leg).

Step and Lower: Take a large step forward (or backward, which is safer for your knees) with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees form a 90-degree angle.

Focus: Shift your weight onto your front (or bent) leg, keeping your back straight and your torso upright.

Return: Push off with your front leg to return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Pendulum Squat
exercises.description: Place your feet in the middle of the plate at about shoulder width. Tense your torso. Keep your neck relaxed.

exercises.name: Lat Pull Down (Straight Back)
exercises.description: The lat pull down is an exercise used to build the muscles of the back. While the exercise will primarily target the lats, you will also notice a fair amount of bicep and middle back activation.
